Inf.description: Positive infinity; -Inf is negative infinity. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Example: 1/0 gives Inf.

MException.description: Creates an error value with identifier, formatted message and an empty stack field, ready to pass to throw. In mylab it is a plain struct, not an object.

NaN.description: Not-a-Number, the result of undefined operations such as 0/0. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. NaN is unequal to everything, itself included; test for it with isnan.

NaT.description: Not-a-Time: the missing value for datetime arrays, as a scalar or an array of the given size. It compares unequal to everything; test for it with isnat.

RandStream.description: Creates a random number stream. Use it with rand(s, ...), randn(s, ...), randi(s, ...) and randperm(s, n), or make it the source for rand/randn/randi with RandStream.setGlobalStream(s). reset(s) starts the sequence again. Properties: Type, Seed, State. Every generator type ('mt19937ar', 'mlfg6331_64', ...) is accepted, but all of them use NumPy's default generator, so the numbers differ from MATLAB's. 'Seed' may be 'shuffle'.

RandStream.create.description: Creates a random number stream; the same as RandStream(type, 'Seed', seed).

RandStream.getGlobalStream.description: Returns the stream that rand, randn and randi currently draw from.

RandStream.list.description: Lists the generator type names RandStream accepts. They all use the same generator in mylab.

RandStream.setGlobalStream.description: Makes s the stream that rand, randn, randi and randperm draw from, and returns the previous one. Example: RandStream.setGlobalStream(RandStream('mt19937ar', 'Seed', 1)).

TriScatteredInterp.description: Older form of scatteredInterpolant. vq = F(xq, yq) interpolates linearly and returns NaN outside the convex hull of the samples.

VideoWriter.description: Creates an object that writes frames to a video file. Typical use: open(v); writeVideo(v, getframe(gcf)) in a loop; close(v). Properties: FrameRate (default 30), Quality (0-100), and read-only Filename, Path, FrameCount, Width, Height, Duration. Profiles 'Motion JPEG AVI' (default, .avi) and 'MPEG-4' (.mp4) need the ffmpeg program; when it is missing an animated GIF with the same base name is written and a warning says so. A file name ending in .gif always writes an animated GIF. The file is produced by close(v).

abs.description: Absolute value of each element; for complex x, the magnitude. Example: abs(3 - 4i) is 5.

usage: A = accumarray(subs, vals, sz, fun, fillval)
accumarray.description: Groups the values vals by the subscripts in subs and combines each group. Each row of subs is one subscript (a column of indices for a vector result, two columns for a matrix, or a cell of index vectors). sz fixes the output size ([] lets the largest subscript decide). fun is called with each group's values as a column and must return a scalar (default: sum); if it returns a cell such as @(x) {x}, the result is a cell array. Positions that receive no values hold fillval (default 0, or [] for cells). Example: accumarray([1; 2; 1], [10; 20; 30], [], @max) is [30; 20].

acos.description: Inverse cosine in radians. Inputs outside [-1, 1] give complex results.

acosh.description: Inverse hyperbolic cosine. Inputs below 1 give complex results.

addOptional.description: Adds an optional positional argument with a default value to the inputParser p. Optional arguments come after the required ones. A text value that is exactly the name of a parameter and starts a complete list of name-value pairs is read as that parameter name, not as the optional value.

addParamValue.description: Older name of addParameter: adds a name-value argument with a default value to the inputParser p.

addParameter.description: Adds a name-value argument with a default value to the inputParser p. Callers pass it as 'Name', value after the positional arguments, or as a field of a struct. Names match without regard to case and may be shortened as long as they stay unique.

addRequired.description: Adds a required positional argument to the inputParser p. validator is a function handle that must return true (or not raise an error) for acceptable values, e.g. @isnumeric or @(x) x > 0.

addSwitch.description: Adds a switch to the inputParser p: p.Results.name is true when the caller passes the name on its own, and false otherwise.

addcats.description: Adds categories to a categorical array, at the end or next to an existing category. No element changes.

addlistener.description: Calls callback(source, eventData) whenever obj fires the event with notify. The second form runs the callback after ('PostSet') or before ('PreSet') the property is assigned; eventData.AffectedObject is the object. Set L.Enabled = false or call delete(L) to stop listening.

addpath.description: Adds folders to the search path used to find .m files and data files. Each argument may hold several folders separated by the path separator (':' or ';'), as genpath returns them. Folders go to the front of the path in the order given, or to the back with '-end'; a folder that is already on the path is moved.

addpoints.description: Appends points to the animated line h and grows the axes limits to include them.

addpref.description: Same as setpref in mylab (an existing preference is replaced).

addtodate.description: Adds a quantity of 'year', 'month', 'week', 'day', 'hour', 'minute', 'second' or 'millisecond' to serial date numbers. Months and years move by calendar, keeping the day of the month where it exists.

addvars.description: Appends variables (columns) to the right of a table.

airy.description: Airy functions: k = 0 gives Ai (default), 1 its derivative, 2 Bi, 3 the derivative of Bi. The third argument 1 returns the exponentially scaled version.

all.description: True if every element is nonzero, tested down columns for a matrix, along dim, or over 'all' elements. all([]) is true.

allchild.description: The objects directly inside the figure, axes or other graphics object h.

allfinite.description: True if no element of A is NaN or infinite.

alpha.description: Sets the transparency of the surfaces, patches and images in the current axes, or of the object h: 0 is clear, 1 is opaque. Per-point modes ('flat', 'interp') are ignored.

amd.description: Minimum-degree style ordering of a symmetric pattern: factorizing A(p, p) usually creates fewer new nonzeros than factorizing A.

ancestor.description: Walks up from h through its parents and returns the first object of the given type, such as 'axes' or 'figure' (h itself when it has that type), or [] when there is none. 'toplevel' returns the highest match instead.

and.description: Same as A & B (element-wise logical AND).

angle.description: Phase angle of each complex element in radians, between -pi and pi.

animatedline.description: Creates a line that grows as points are added with addpoints, without clearing the axes. Options: Color, LineWidth, LineStyle, Marker, MaximumNumPoints (older points are dropped beyond this number). Example: h = animatedline; for k = 1:50, addpoints(h, k, sin(k/5)); drawnow; end

annotation.description: Draws a shape on the figure (not tied to axes) in normalized figure units from 0 to 1. x = [x1 x2] and y = [y1 y2] give the start and end points; pos = [left bottom width height].

anova1.description: One-way analysis of variance: tests whether several groups share the same mean. Groups are the columns of y, or are given by labels in group (numbers, a char matrix or a cell array). tbl is the ANOVA table as a cell array; stats holds the group names, sizes and means. No figure is shown.

any.description: True if at least one element is nonzero, tested down columns for a matrix (a row of results), along dim, or over 'all' elements. any([]) is false.

anynan.description: True if any element of A is NaN.

appdesigner.description: Not available. .mlapp files are binary and cannot be opened; export the app to a .m file in MATLAB and run that. The mylab web app has its own app builder (New app).

area.description: Plots the curve y and shades the region between it and zero. Only a single vector is supported. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

array2table.description: Turns each column of the matrix A into a table variable.

arrayfun.description: Calls f on each element of one or more same-size arrays, the way cellfun does for cells. Elements of a struct array are passed as 1-by-1 structs and elements of a cell array as 1-by-1 cells. Example: arrayfun(@(k) k^2, 1:3) is [1 4 9].

asin.description: Inverse sine in radians. Inputs outside [-1, 1] give complex results.

asinh.description: Inverse hyperbolic sine of each element.

assert.description: Throws an error if cond is false (or not all true). The default message is 'Assertion failed.'; a custom message and identifier follow the same rules as error.

assignin.description: Assigns value to the variable name in another workspace: 'base' (the top-level workspace) or 'caller' (the function that called the current one).

atan.description: Inverse tangent in radians, between -pi/2 and pi/2. See atan2 for the full circle.

atan2.description: Four-quadrant angle in radians, between -pi and pi, of the point (x, y). Note that y comes first. Inputs expand against each other. Example: atan2(1, -1) is 3*pi/4.

atan2d.description: Four-quadrant inverse tangent like atan2, but the result is in degrees.

atanh.description: Inverse hyperbolic tangent. Inputs outside (-1, 1) give complex or infinite results.

audioinfo.description: Returns a struct describing a sound file: Filename, NumChannels, SampleRate, TotalSamples, Duration (seconds) and BitsPerSample. Only WAV files are supported.

audioplayer.description: Creates a player object for the samples y. play(p), playblocking(p), pause(p), resume(p) and stop(p) are accepted but play nothing: mylab has no audio device. Properties: SampleRate, TotalSamples, NumChannels, BitsPerSample.

audioread.description: Reads a sound file: y has one row per sample and one column per channel, scaled to the range -1 to 1, and Fs is the sample rate in Hz. [first last] reads part of the file; 'native' returns the stored integer type. Only WAV files are supported.

audiowrite.description: Writes the samples y (one column per channel, values from -1 to 1) to a WAV file with sample rate Fs. BitsPerSample is 8, 16 (default), 24, 32 or 64. Values outside -1 to 1 are clipped with a warning. Only WAV files are supported.

autumn.description: n-by-3 colormap from red through orange to yellow.

axes.description: Creates new axes in the current figure and makes them current; Position is given as fractions of the figure (use it for insets), and other axes properties can follow as name/value pairs. axes(ax) makes existing axes current. A figure handle as first input or 'Parent' chooses the figure.

usage: axis([xmin xmax ymin ymax zmin zmax])
axis.description: Sets axis limits or appearance. An Inf or -Inf limit keeps that end automatic, e.g. axis([0 Inf 0 Inf]). 'equal' makes units the same length on both axes, 'image' does that and fits the data tightly, 'square' makes the plot box square, 'tight' fits the limits to the data, 'off' hides the axes, 'auto' restores automatic limits, 'normal' also undoes 'equal' and 'square', 'ij' puts the y origin at the top and 'xy' back at the bottom. With an output and no input, returns the current limits.

bandwidth.description: Number of nonzero diagonals below (lower) and above (upper) the main diagonal.

bar.description: Vertical bar chart of y, at positions x or 1..n. A matrix y draws groups of bars, one group per row and one colour per column, or stacks them with 'stacked'. width is the fraction of the space each group fills (default 0.8). Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, LineWidth, FaceAlpha, DisplayName. b is a Bar handle (a row array of them for a matrix y).

barh.description: Horizontal bar chart; takes the same inputs and options as bar.

base2dec.description: Number written by the text s in the given base (2 to 36). A char matrix or cell array gives a column of numbers; text that is not a valid number gives NaN.

beep.description: Accepted for compatibility; makes no sound.

besseli.description: Modified Bessel function of the first kind I_nu(z); 1 returns the exponentially scaled form.

besselj.description: Bessel function of the first kind J_nu(z), element by element. The third argument 1 returns the exponentially scaled version. Results may be complex for negative z.

besselk.description: Modified Bessel function of the second kind K_nu(z); 1 returns the exponentially scaled form.

bessely.description: Bessel function of the second kind Y_nu(z). Negative z gives complex results; 1 scales.

beta.description: Beta function, gamma(a).*gamma(b)./gamma(a+b), element by element.

betacdf.description: Beta distribution cumulative probability. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

betainc.description: Regularized incomplete beta function for x in [0, 1], lower tail by default or upper tail with 'upper'.

betapdf.description: Beta distribution density on [0, 1] with shape parameters a and b.

betarnd.description: Random numbers from the beta distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. betarnd(a, b, 3, 2) or betarnd(a, b, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

between.description: The calendar duration from t1 to t2, as whole months, then days, then the remaining time, so that t1 + c equals t2.

bicg.description: Solves A*x = b with the biconjugate gradient method. A must be a matrix (the method also needs A'), and preconditioners are not used. tol defaults to 1e-6 and maxit to min(n, 20).

usage: x = bicgstab(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
bicgstab.description: Solves A*x = b for a general square A with the stabilized biconjugate gradient method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed.

bin2dec.description: Value of a binary digit string; spaces are ignored. A char matrix or cell array gives a column of numbers. Example: bin2dec('101') is 5.

binocdf.description: Binomial probability of at most x successes in n trials. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

binopdf.description: Binomial probability of exactly x successes in n trials with success probability p. Example: binopdf(1, 2, 0.5) is 0.5.

binornd.description: Binomial random counts for n trials with probability p.

bitand.description: Bitwise AND of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

bitcmp.description: Bitwise complement of non-negative integers within the width of the integer class (8, 16, 32 or 64 bits).

bitget.description: Value (0 or 1) of bit number bit (1 = least significant) of each non-negative integer in a. Example: bitget(6, 1:3) is [0 1 1].

bitor.description: Bitwise OR of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

bitset.description: Sets bit number bit of a to 1 (or to value, 0 or 1). Example: bitset(8, 1) is 9.

bitshift.description: Shifts the bits of integer values left by n places (right when n is negative). n must be a scalar. Example: bitshift(1, 3) is 8.

bitxor.description: Bitwise exclusive OR of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

blackman.description: Blackman window of length n as a column vector.

blkdiag.description: Block-diagonal matrix with A1, A2, ... along the diagonal and zeros elsewhere. The result is sparse when any input is sparse.

bone.description: n-by-3 greyscale colormap with a slight blue tint.

bounds.description: Smallest and largest elements of x in one call, ignoring NaN. mylab always looks at all elements; a dimension argument is not supported.

box.description: Shows or hides the top and right edges of the current axes' frame; box alone toggles. The axes property Box does the same.

boxchart.description: Box-and-whisker plot; drawn like boxplot in mylab.

boxplot.description: Box-and-whisker plot. Each column of x is one box, or the values of a vector x are split by the grouping variable. Options: 'Labels', 'Notch', 'Whisker', 'Widths', 'Positions', 'Orientation' ('horizontal').

brush.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

bsxfun.description: Expands singleton dimensions of A and B so their sizes match, then calls the binary function f once with the expanded arrays. Plain operators already expand like this, e.g. A - mean(A).

builtin.description: Calls the built-in function with that name, even when a file or class method with the same name exists.

butter.description: Butterworth filter design (maximally flat IIR filter) of order n. Wn is the cutoff as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency (between 0 and 1); a two-element Wn designs a band-pass filter. ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass' or 'stop'. 's' designs an analog filter with Wn in rad/s. Example: [b, a] = butter(4, 0.2) is a 4th-order low-pass filter for use with filter.

bwareaopen.description: Removes connected groups with fewer than p pixels from a binary image.

bwboundaries.description: Traces the outer boundary of each object in a binary image (8-connected). B is a cell array with one k-by-2 matrix of [row column] points per object, going clockwise and ending at its starting point; L is the label matrix and n the number of objects. Boundaries of holes inside objects are not traced, with or without 'noholes'.

bwconncomp.description: Connected components of a 2-D binary image as a struct with fields Connectivity, ImageSize, NumObjects and PixelIdxList (a cell with the linear indices of each component).

bwdist.description: Distance from every pixel to the nearest true pixel, as single. method is 'euclidean' (default), 'cityblock', 'chessboard' or 'quasi-euclidean'. idx is the linear index of that nearest pixel.

bwlabel.description: Labels the connected groups of true pixels in a binary image with 1, 2, ..., n (0 is background). conn is 8 (default; diagonal neighbours touch) or 4. Groups are numbered in the order their first pixel appears going down the columns.

bwmorph.description: Applies a binary morphological operation n times (once by default; Inf repeats until nothing changes). Operations: 'thin' and 'skel' (reduce shapes to one-pixel-wide lines, both by Zhang-Suen thinning), 'remove' (keep outlines), 'clean' (drop isolated pixels), 'fill' (fill isolated holes), 'majority', 'bridge', 'diag', 'spur', 'endpoints', 'branchpoints', 'dilate', 'erode', 'open', 'close', 'perim4' and 'perim8'. Thinned shapes can differ by a few pixels from other implementations.

bwperim.description: Outline of the objects in a binary image: true pixels that touch a false pixel or the image border (4-connected by default).

caldays.description: A calendar duration of n calendar days (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

caldiff.description: Calendar durations between successive elements of a datetime vector.

calendar.description: Shows the calendar of a month (the current one by default), or returns it as a 6-by-7 matrix with weeks as rows starting on Sunday and zeros for days outside the month.

calmonths.description: A calendar duration of n calendar months (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

calquarters.description: A calendar duration of n calendar quarters (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

calweeks.description: A calendar duration of n calendar weeks (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

calyears.description: A calendar duration of n calendar years (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

camlight.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. An output, if requested, is [].

canUseGPU.description: Always false: mylab does not use GPUs.

canUseParallelPool.description: Always false: mylab runs everything in one process.

cart2pol.description: Converts Cartesian coordinates to polar (or cylindrical): theta is the angle in radians and rho the distance from the origin. A single matrix with 2 or 3 columns may be given and, with one output, a matrix of the same layout is returned.

cart2sph.description: Converts Cartesian coordinates to spherical: azimuth in the x-y plane, elevation from that plane (both in radians) and radius.

cast.description: Converts x to the named class: 'double', 'single', 'logical', 'char' or an integer class. cast(x, 'like', p) converts to the class of p.

cat.description: Joins arrays along dimension dim: 1 stacks them vertically, 2 side by side, 3 stacks them as pages of an N-D array, and so on. Sizes must agree in every other dimension.

categorical.description: Creates a categorical array: each element is one of a fixed list of named categories. values can be numbers, logical values, a cell array of text or a string array. Without valueset the categories are the sorted distinct values; empty text and NaN become <undefined>. names gives the category name for each allowed value. Compare with text (c == 'red'), count with countcats, list with categories. Ordinal arrays also support < and >. Assigning a new name adds a category. Works as a table variable and as a grouping variable for groupsummary, findgroups and grp2idx. Example: c = categorical({'red', 'blue', 'red'})

categories.description: Returns the category names of a categorical array as a cell array (a column), in category order. Example: c = categorical({'red', 'blue', 'red'}); categories(c) gives {'blue'; 'red'}.

caxis.description: Sets the data values mapped to the first and last colormap colours of the current axes (surfaces, images, filled contours and scatter colours); 'auto' returns to the data range, and with no input the current limits are returned. clim is the newer name. Call it after plotting.

cd.description: Changes the current working folder (a leading ~ means your home folder). With no input, prints or returns the current folder.

ceil.description: Rounds each element up, toward +Inf. Example: ceil(2.1) is 3.

cell.description: Cell array whose cells all hold the empty matrix []. cell(n) is n-by-n.

cell2mat.description: Concatenates the contents of a cell array into one array, joining each row of cells side by side and then stacking the rows. The pieces must fit together. Example: cell2mat({1 2; 3 4}) is [1 2; 3 4].

cell2struct.description: Builds a scalar struct whose fields, named by a cell array (or a single name), take their values from the cells of C in order. A dimension argument and struct-array results are not supported.

cell2table.description: Makes a table with one variable per column of the cell array C. Columns holding only numeric scalars become numeric variables; others stay cell columns.

celldisp.description: Prints the contents of every cell, labelled like C{1} or C{2,3}, descending into nested cell arrays. name replaces the label 'C'.

cellfun.description: Calls f on the contents of each cell (on matching cells of several same-size inputs). By default every call must return a scalar and the results form an array the size of C; with 'UniformOutput' false they are collected in a cell array. f may be a handle or a function name; the names 'isempty', 'length', 'numel', 'isreal', 'islogical' and 'ndims' are handled directly. An error handler h is called with an error struct and the inputs. Example: cellfun(@numel, {'ab', 'c'}) is [2 1].

cellstr.description: Converts text to a cell array of char vectors: each row of a char matrix becomes one cell (trailing blanks removed), giving a column; a string array gives a cell array of the same size (<missing> becomes ''); a cell array is returned as is.

usage: x = cgs(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
cgs.description: Solves A*x = b for a general square A with the conjugate gradient squared method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed.

char.description: Makes a char array. Numbers are taken as character codes. A cell array, a string array or several text inputs become rows of a char matrix, padded with spaces to equal length. Example: char(72, 105) is a two-row char array; char([72 105]) is 'Hi'.

cheby1.description: Chebyshev Type I filter design: order n, Rp decibels of ripple allowed in the passband, and a sharper roll-off than Butterworth. Wn and ftype work as in butter.

chi2cdf.description: Chi-square cumulative probability with nu degrees of freedom. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

chi2pdf.description: Chi-square density with nu degrees of freedom.

chi2rnd.description: Random numbers from the chi-square (v degrees of freedom) distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. chi2rnd(v, 3, 2) or chi2rnd(v, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

usage: y = chirp(t, f0, t1, f1, method)
y = chirp(t, f0, t1, f1, method, phi)
chirp.description: Swept-frequency cosine whose frequency moves from f0 at time 0 to f1 at time t1 (defaults 0, 1 and 100 Hz). method is 'linear' (default), 'quadratic' or 'logarithmic'; phi is the initial phase in degrees.

chol.description: Cholesky factor of a symmetric positive definite matrix: upper triangular R with R'*R = A, or lower triangular L with L*L' = A. If A is not positive definite it is an error, unless p is requested: then p is nonzero and R is empty (mylab does not return a partial factor).

circshift.description: Shifts elements circularly by k places, wrapping the ones that fall off the end back to the start. Without dim the shift follows the first dimension whose size is not 1; a two-element shift moves rows and columns. Example: circshift([1 2 3], 1) is [3 1 2].

cla.description: Removes everything drawn in the current axes, keeping the figure and any other axes.

clabel.description: Writes the level values on the lines of a contour plot, where [C, h] came from contour or contourf. With C alone the most recent contour plot of the current axes is labelled.

class.description: Name of the type of x as a char vector, for example 'double', 'char', 'logical', 'int8', 'cell', 'struct', 'string' or 'function_handle'. Objects report their class name, such as 'table', 'containers.Map' or the name of a classdef class.

clc.description: Clears the command window when the host program supports it; otherwise does nothing.

clear.description: Removes variables from the current workspace: all of them, the named ones, or those matching a wildcard pattern. 'clear all' also clears globals and closes figures; 'clear global' removes global variables. 'clear functions' is accepted and does nothing.

clearpoints.description: Removes all points from the animated line h.

clearvars.description: Removes variables from the current workspace: all of them, the named ones, or those matching a wildcard pattern. 'clear all' also clears globals and closes figures; 'clear global' removes global variables. 'clear functions' is accepted and does nothing.

clf.description: Clears everything from the current figure, or from figure handle f.

clim.description: Sets the data values mapped to the first and last colormap colours of the current axes (surfaces, images, filled contours and scatter colours); 'auto' returns to the data range, and with no input the current limits are returned. clim is the newer name. Call it after plotting.

clock.description: The current local date and time as [year month day hour minute seconds].

close.description: Closes the current figure, figure number n, the figure with handle f or with that Name, or all figures. close(v) finishes the file of a VideoWriter, and close(h) dismisses a waitbar or message box.

closereq.description: Deletes the window whose callback is running (the default CloseRequestFcn).

colamd.description: Column ordering that reduces fill-in when A(:, p) is factorized.

colon.description: Function form of the a:b and a:step:b range operators. Returns a row vector, empty when the range runs the wrong way or the step is 0.

colorbar.description: Adds a colour scale beside the current axes for the most recent image, surface or contour plot (or for the colormap alone). location is 'eastoutside' (default), 'westoutside', 'northoutside' or 'southoutside'. c is a ColorBar handle: c.Label.String sets its label, and Limits, Ticks, TickLabels and FontSize can be read and set. colorbar off removes it.

colormap.description: Sets the colour map of the current figure, recolouring its images and surfaces and those drawn later. name is a colormap name such as 'parula' (the default, drawn with matplotlib's viridis), 'jet', 'hot', 'gray' or any matplotlib colormap; map is an m-by-3 matrix of RGB values in [0, 1], e.g. jet(16). target may be an axes or figure handle. With an output, returns the current map as a matrix (256 rows for named maps).

comet.description: Draws the curve as an ordinary line plot; the moving-head animation is not reproduced.

comet3.description: Draws the 3-D curve as an ordinary plot3 line, without the animation.

compan.description: Companion matrix of the polynomial with coefficients p (highest power first). Its eigenvalues are the roots of the polynomial.

complex.description: Builds a complex array a + b*i. With one input the imaginary part is zero but the result is still stored as complex, so isreal reports false.

compose.description: Formats data into text with sprintf-style conversions, giving one piece of text per row rather than one long result. With a single array, each row is fed to the format, using as many columns per piece as the format has conversions; with several arrays, matching elements are formatted together. Returns a cell array of char vectors, or a string array when fmt is a string. Example: compose('%d-%d', [1 2; 3 4]) is {'1-2'; '3-4'}.

computer.description: Name of the platform as reported by Python, e.g. 'linux', 'darwin' or 'win32'. These codes differ from the architecture strings other implementations use.

cond.description: 2-norm condition number, the ratio of the largest to smallest singular value. Large values mean that solving with A loses accuracy. Other norms are not supported.

condest.description: Estimate of the 1-norm condition number of a square matrix, computed from a sparse LU factorization. A singular matrix gives Inf.

conj.description: Complex conjugate of each element: the sign of the imaginary part is flipped.

containers.Map.description: Creates a map from keys (char vectors or numbers) to values. Read and write entries with m(key) and m(key) = value; use keys(m), values(m), isKey(m, k), remove(m, k) and m.Count. A map is a handle: copying the variable shares the same map.

contains.description: True if s contains pattern anywhere. pattern may be a cell or string array, meaning any of them. s may be a cell or string array, giving a logical array.

contour.description: Draws contour lines (lines of equal height) of Z, optionally over the grid X, Y, with n levels or at the given level values (also 'LevelList'). 'ShowText', 'on' labels the lines; 'LineColor' and 'LineWidth' style them. Replaces the current axes unless hold is on. With two outputs, C is the contour matrix (for each line a column [level; count] followed by the x and y coordinates) and h the Contour handle.

contourf.description: Like contour, but fills the regions between the contour lines with colour.

conv.description: Convolution of two vectors, which is also polynomial multiplication. shape is 'full' (default, length numel(u)+numel(v)-1), 'same' (central part the size of u) or 'valid'. The result is a column if u is a column. Example: conv([1 1], [1 -1]) is [1 0 -1].

conv2.description: Two-dimensional convolution. shape 'full' (default) returns the whole result, 'same' the central part with the size of A, and 'valid' only the part computed without zero padding. With two vectors u and v, A is convolved with column u and then with row v.

convertCharsToStrings.description: Converts char arrays to string scalars and cell arrays of char vectors to string arrays. Other values are returned unchanged.

convertStringsToChars.description: Converts string scalars to char vectors and string arrays to cell arrays of char vectors. Other values are returned unchanged.

convertTo.description: Converts a datetime array to numbers: kind is 'datenum', 'posixtime', 'excel', 'juliandate', 'modifiedjuliandate' or 'yyyymmdd'.

convhull.description: Convex hull. In 2-D, k lists the corner points counterclockwise, starting from the leftmost point and ending where it starts, so plot(x(k), y(k)) draws the hull; v is the area. In 3-D, each row of k is a triangle of the hull surface and v the volume. Points that are all on one line (or plane) raise an error.

convhulln.description: Convex hull of the points in the rows of P in any dimension: each row of K is a facet, v the enclosed volume.

convn.description: N-dimensional convolution. shape is 'full' (default), 'same' (the central part, the size of A) or 'valid' (only where B fits completely inside A).

cool.description: n-by-3 colormap from cyan to magenta.

copper.description: n-by-3 colormap from black to a light copper colour.

copyfile.description: Copies a file or a whole folder. source may contain wildcards (*), and destination may be a folder; existing files are overwritten. With outputs, [status, message, messageId] report success (true) or the reason for failure instead of raising an error.

copyobj.description: Copies 2-D line objects into the axes ax and returns the copies. Other kinds of object cannot be copied in mylab.

corr.description: Linear (Pearson, default) or rank (Spearman) correlation between the columns of X, or between each column of X and each column of Y. Kendall's tau is not supported.

corr2.description: Correlation coefficient between two arrays of the same size.

corrcoef.description: Pearson correlation coefficients between the columns of X (or between x and y), with ones on the diagonal. P holds p-values for testing zero correlation. Name-value options are ignored.

cos.description: Cosine of each element, with x in radians.

cosd.description: Cosine of angles given in degrees. Odd multiples of 90 give exactly 0.

count.description: Number of non-overlapping occurrences of pattern (or of any pattern in a list) in s. A cell array of text gives an array of counts. Example: count('banana', 'an') is 2.

countcats.description: Number of elements in each category of a categorical array, in category order.

cov.description: Covariance. For a vector, the variance; for a matrix whose columns are variables, the covariance matrix; for two vectors, their 2-by-2 covariance matrix. w = 1 normalizes by N instead of N-1. 'omitrows' drops rows containing NaN.

cputime.description: Processor time used by mylab so far, in seconds. Differences between two calls time code.

createCallbackFcn.description: Part of the code App Designer exports: returns a callback that calls method(app, event), or method(app) when passEvent is false.

cross.description: Cross product of two 3-element vectors, shaped like a. Matrix inputs are not supported. Example: cross([1 0 0], [0 1 0]) is [0 0 1].

csvread.description: Reads a comma-separated numeric file; empty fields become 0. r and c are zero-based row and column offsets of the first value to read.

csvwrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix as comma-separated values with five significant digits; r and c shift the data down and right, padding with zeros.

ctranspose.description: Same as A' : swaps rows and columns and conjugates complex values.

cummax.description: Running maximum along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. Example: cummax([1 3 2 5]) is [1 3 3 5].

cummin.description: Running minimum along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

cumprod.description: Running product along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

cumsum.description: Running total along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. 'reverse' accumulates from the end. Integer inputs keep their class and saturate. NaN flags are accepted but have no effect. Example: cumsum([1 2 3]) is [1 3 6].

cumtrapz.description: Running trapezoid-rule integral, same size as y and starting at 0. Uses unit spacing or the points in x, along the first dimension whose size is not 1.

cylinder.description: Coordinates of a cylinder of height 1 with n points around (default 20). r is the radius, or a vector of radii along the height for a surface of revolution. Without outputs it draws the surface.

daspect.description: Sets the relative length of one data unit along x, y and z; daspect([1 1 1]) draws circles as circles, like axis equal. In 3-D only equal ratios have an effect.

datacursormode.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

datasample.description: Picks k random elements of a vector, or k random rows of a matrix or table (columns with dim = 2). Sampling is with replacement unless 'Replace', false. idx are the positions that were picked.

date.description: Today's date as text in the form '15-Mar-2024'.

usage: n = datenum(Y, M, D, H, MI, S)
n = datenum([Y M D H MI S])
datenum.description: Converts dates to serial date numbers. A serial date number counts days from year 0, with the time of day as the fraction. Input can be a datetime array, date text (optionally with a datestr-style format), separate components, or a matrix of date vectors.

dateshift.description: Moves each datetime to the start or end of the unit of time that contains it: 'year', 'quarter', 'month', 'week' (weeks start on Sunday), 'day', 'hour', 'minute' or 'second'. The end of a year, quarter, month or week is its last day; the end of a shorter unit is the instant the next one begins. rule is 'current' (default), 'next', 'previous', 'nearest' or a whole number of units to move. With 'dayofweek', moves to the given weekday (a name or 1-7 with 1 = Sunday) on or after t ('next', default), on or before t ('previous') or closest to t ('nearest').

datestr.description: Formats dates as text. t can be serial date numbers, date vectors, datetimes or date text; several dates give one row of text each. The default is 'dd-mmm-yyyy HH:MM:SS', or just the date when every time is midnight. Format numbers 0 to 31 select standard layouts (for example 1 is 'dd-mmm-yyyy', 13 is 'HH:MM:SS', 29 is 'yyyy-mm-dd' and 31 is 'yyyy-mm-dd HH:MM:SS'). A free format uses yyyy, yy, mmmm, mmm, mm (month), dddd, ddd, dd, HH, MM (minute), SS, FFF (milliseconds) and AM or PM for a 12-hour clock.

usage: t = datetime(Y, M, D, H, MI, S)
datetime.description: Creates an array of points in time. Numeric inputs give the year, month, day and optionally the hour, minute and second (scalars or arrays of one size; out-of-range values roll over). Text (a char vector, string array or cell array of text) is parsed: ISO forms such as '2024-03-15 10:30:00' and common forms such as '15-Mar-2024', '03/15/2024' or 'March 15, 2024' are recognized automatically, and 'InputFormat' states the layout explicitly. 'ConvertFrom' accepts 'datenum', 'posixtime', 'excel', 'juliandate', 'modifiedjuliandate', 'yyyymmdd' and 'epochtime'. 'Format' sets how values are shown, using the letters y (year), M (month: MM number, MMM short name, MMMM full name), d (day), e (weekday: eee short, eeee full), H (hour 0-23), h (hour 1-12), m (minute), s (second), S (fraction of a second), a (AM/PM), with literal text in single quotes. 'TimeZone' may be 'UTC', 'local' or '' (none); other zones are not available. Properties Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Format and TimeZone can be read and set. Datetimes support subtraction (giving a duration), adding durations and calendar durations, comparison, sorting, indexing and concatenation; NaT marks a missing value.

datetime.empty.description: An empty datetime array (0-by-0 by default).

usage: [Y, M, D, H, MI, S] = datevec(t)
datevec.description: Splits dates into components. Each row of v is [year month day hour minute second]. t can be serial date numbers, date text or datetimes.

day.description: Day of the month of each element of a datetime array. Options give the day of the year, the day of the week (1 is Sunday) or the weekday names ('name' or 'shortname').

days.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many 24-hour days. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of 24-hour days.

dbcont.description: At the K>> prompt: continue running until the next breakpoint.

dbdown.description: Not supported: the K>> prompt always works in the paused function's workspace.

dbquit.description: At the K>> prompt: stop the program.

dbstack.description: Shows the functions currently being run, innermost first, or returns them as a struct array.

dbstatus.description: Lists the breakpoints, or returns them as a struct array.

dbstep.description: At the K>> prompt: run the next line (stepping over calls), step into a function, or run until the current function returns.

dbstop.description: Sets a breakpoint: the program pauses with a K>> prompt when it reaches that line. Needs an interactive terminal. In the web app, use Step through instead.

dbup.description: Not supported: the K>> prompt always works in the paused function's workspace.

deal.description: Copies inputs to outputs: one input is copied to every output; otherwise there must be as many inputs as outputs and each goes to its own output.

deblank.description: Removes trailing whitespace and null characters only.

dec2base.description: Text for the non-negative integer d in the given base (2 to 36), with at least n digits. An array gives a char matrix with one row per number. A char vector of symbols can be given instead of the base.

dec2bin.description: Binary digits of the non-negative integer d as text, with at least n digits. An array gives a char matrix with one row per number. Example: dec2bin(5) is '101'.

dec2hex.description: Hexadecimal digits (upper case) of the non-negative integer d as text, with at least n digits. An array gives a char matrix with one row per number. Example: dec2hex(255) is 'FF'.

decimate.description: Reduces the sample rate by the integer factor r after low-pass filtering: by default an 8th-order Chebyshev Type I filter applied forward and backward (zero phase), or a 30-tap FIR filter with 'fir'. n changes the filter order.

deconv.description: Polynomial division: b = conv(a, q) + r. r has the same length as b, padded with leading zeros.

deg2rad.description: Converts angles from degrees to radians (multiplies by pi/180).

del2.description: Discrete Laplacian. For a vector it is one quarter of the second difference; for a matrix it is (d2U/dx2 + d2U/dy2)/4. Values on the edges are extrapolated from the interior. h, hx and hy are scalar spacings between points (default 1).

delaunay.description: Delaunay triangulation. Each row of T holds the point numbers of one triangle (counterclockwise), or of one tetrahedron in 3-D. Draw it with triplot(T, x, y) or trisurf(T, x, y, z).

delaunayn.description: Delaunay triangulation of the points in the rows of P, in any dimension.

delete.description: Deletes the named file(s), or, for a handle object, runs the class's delete method (if any) and marks the object invalid so later use raises an error. For graphics handles (from plot, figure, legend, ...) the object is removed from its plot; deleting a figure closes it.

det.description: Determinant of a square matrix. Example: det([1 2; 3 4]) is -2.

detrend.description: Removes the best-fit straight line (default), mean ('constant') or polynomial of degree n from a vector or from each column of a matrix. Breakpoints are not supported.

deval.description: Evaluates a solution structure from an ODE solver at the times t, using the solver's own continuous interpolant, so the values are as accurate as the solution itself. Each column of y is the state at one time; idx selects components and yp holds the derivatives. Times must lie within the solved interval.

diag.description: For a vector v, builds a square matrix with v on the k-th diagonal (k = 0 main, k > 0 above, k < 0 below). For a matrix A, extracts the k-th diagonal as a column vector. Example: diag([1 2]) is [1 0; 0 2].

dialog.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

diary.description: Records everything printed in the command window in a text file. diary on appends to the file named 'diary' in the current folder (or the name set earlier), diary(filename) switches to that file and turns recording on, diary off stops, and diary alone toggles. Typed commands are not recorded, only output.

diff.description: Differences between neighbouring elements, x(2)-x(1), x(3)-x(2), ..., along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given. n repeats the operation n times, so the result is n elements shorter. Example: diff([1 4 9]) is [3 5].

dir.description: Lists a folder, the files matching a wildcard pattern such as '*.csv', or a single file. With an output, returns a column struct array with fields name, folder, date, bytes, isdir and datenum. A folder listing includes '.' and '..'.

disp.description: Print the value of x without showing a variable name. An empty char prints a blank line; other empty values print nothing. Example: disp('hello') prints hello.

display.description: Prints x the way an unterminated statement would, with an 'ans =' header.

dlmread.description: Reads a delimited numeric file; empty fields become 0. r and c are zero-based offsets.

dlmwrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix to a delimited text file (comma by default; '\t' or 'tab' for tabs). precision is a number of significant digits or a format such as '%.3f' (default five significant digits).

doc.description: Same as help: prints the help text in the command window (no browser is opened).

dos.description: Same as system, kept for code written for Windows.

dot.description: Dot product. For two vectors with the same number of elements, sum(conj(a).*b); for matrices, the dot products of matching columns as a row vector. A dim argument is not supported.

double.description: Converts to double precision. Char input gives character codes; a string or string array is parsed as numbers element by element (NaN where the text is not a number or is <missing>). Cells and structs cannot be converted. Example: double('A') is 65; double("2.5") is 2.5.

downsample.description: Keeps every n-th sample of x, starting with the first (or after skipping phase samples).

drawnow.description: Updates figure windows so that pending drawing appears, e.g. inside an animation loop. Options such as limitrate are accepted. Where there is no live window (browser app, Jupyter, MCP, --no-plots) each call records a snapshot of the current figure, and the snapshots of a run are returned as an animated GIF. shg and refresh do the same.

dsearchn.description: For each row of Q, the row number of the nearest point in X and the distance to it.

duration.description: Creates an array of lengths of time from hours, minutes and seconds (and optionally milliseconds), or from text such as '01:30:00' or '2:12:00:00' (days:hours:minutes:seconds). The Format property controls the display: 'hh:mm:ss' (default), 'dd:hh:mm:ss', 'mm:ss', 'hh:mm', fractional seconds as in 'hh:mm:ss.SSS', or a single unit 'y', 'd', 'h', 'm' or 's'. Durations can be added, subtracted, compared, scaled by numbers and divided by each other (giving a number). In arithmetic with a duration, a plain number counts as days.

duration.empty.description: An empty duration array (0-by-0 by default).

e.description: Euler's number 2.71828..., the base of the natural logarithm. Same as exp(1).

edge.description: Finds edges in a grayscale image and returns them as a binary image. Methods: 'sobel' (default), 'prewitt' and 'roberts' threshold the gradient magnitude and thin the result ('nothinning' skips that; direction 'horizontal' or 'vertical' limits the search); 'log' marks zero crossings after a Laplacian-of-Gaussian filter (sigma 2); 'canny' smooths (sigma sqrt(2)), keeps ridges of the gradient and links weak edges to strong ones, with thresholds [low high]. Thresholds are chosen automatically when omitted. Edge maps agree closely with other implementations but individual pixels may differ.

eig.description: Eigenvalues of a square matrix as a column vector, or eigenvector matrix V and diagonal eigenvalue matrix D with A*V = V*D. With B, solves the generalized problem A*V = B*V*D. Symmetric (Hermitian) input gets real eigenvalues in ascending order; for other matrices the order and eigenvector scaling may differ from other implementations.

eigs.description: A few eigenvalues of a large (usually sparse) square matrix: the k largest in magnitude by default (k = 6). sigma chooses which ones: 'largestabs' ('lm'), 'smallestabs' ('sm'), 'largestreal', 'smallestreal', 'bothendsreal', or a number to get the eigenvalues closest to it. With two outputs the columns of V are eigenvectors and D is a diagonal matrix. A second matrix B solves the generalized problem A*v = lambda*B*v. Function-handle operators are not supported.

ellipke.description: Complete elliptic integrals of the first (K) and second (E) kind for parameter m in [0, 1]. A tolerance argument is not supported.

usage: [X, Y, Z] = ellipsoid(xc, yc, zc, xr, yr, zr)
ellipsoid.description: Coordinates of an ellipsoid with center (xc, yc, zc) and semi-axes xr, yr, zr, as (n+1)-by-(n+1) matrices (n = 20 by default). Without outputs it draws the surface.

endsWith.description: True if s ends with pattern (or any pattern in a cell array). Works element-wise on a cell array s.

entropy.description: Entropy of a grayscale image in bits, -sum(p .* log2(p)) over its 256-bin histogram.

enumeration.description: Lists the members of an enumeration class (a classdef with an enumeration block), or returns them as an object array together with their names.

envelope.description: Upper and lower envelopes of a signal from the magnitude of its analytic signal, centred on the mean. Only the 'analytic' method is supported; a window length argument is ignored.

eomday.description: Last day of the given month, taking leap years into account: eomday(2024, 2) is 29.

eps.description: With no input, the gap between 1 and the next larger double, about 2.2204e-16. eps(x) gives that gap at the magnitude of each element of x. eps('single') gives the single-precision gap.

erase.description: Deletes every occurrence of pattern (or of each pattern in a list) from the text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output. Example: erase('a-b-c', '-') is 'abc'.

erfc.description: Complementary error function, 1 - erf(x), accurate for large x.

erfcinv.description: Inverse complementary error function; defined for y in [0, 2].

erfinv.description: Inverse error function; defined for y in [-1, 1].

error.description: Throws an error that stops the program unless caught by try/catch. The message is formatted like sprintf when extra arguments or escapes are present. A first argument such as 'pkg:name' (with a colon and no spaces) followed by more text is taken as the identifier. A struct with message and identifier fields can be passed instead. error([]) does nothing.

errorbar.description: Plots y with vertical error bars, of half-length err or with separate lower and upper lengths neg and pos. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

errordlg.description: Prints the message with the label 'Error' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines. The script continues; use error to stop it.

etime.description: Seconds elapsed from date vector t0 to date vector t1 ([year month day hour minute seconds], as returned by clock).

eval.description: Runs text as code in the current workspace. If it fails and catchcode is given, that is run instead. With outputs, code must be a single expression whose values are returned. Building variable names with eval is error-prone; prefer arrays, cells or structs.

evalc.description: Runs text as code and returns everything it would have printed, as a char vector.

evalin.description: Runs code or evaluates an expression in the 'base' or 'caller' workspace, so it sees and changes the variables there. A third argument is run if the first raises an error.

event.EventData.description: Creates an empty event data object with the properties Source and EventName. Classes that carry extra data with an event derive from it: classdef MyData < event.EventData.

exceltime.description: Spreadsheet serial day numbers (day 1 is January 1, 1900) for each datetime.

exist.description: Tells what a name refers to: 1 for a variable, 2 for a file or a function defined in a .m file or in the session, 5 for a built-in function, 7 for a folder, 0 if not found. kind ('var', 'file', 'dir' or 'builtin') limits the search.

exit.description: Ends the mylab session, optionally with a numeric exit status for the operating system.

exp.description: e raised to the power of each element. Example: exp(0) is 1.

expcdf.description: Exponential cumulative probability with mean mu (default 1). Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

expint.description: Exponential integral E1(x), the integral of exp(-t)/t from x to Inf. Negative real x gives complex results.

expm.description: Matrix exponential of a square matrix (not the element-wise exp).

expm1.description: exp(x) - 1 computed accurately when x is tiny.

exportgraphics.description: Saves the figure containing obj (a figure or axes handle, e.g. gcf or gca) to an image file, with the format taken from the extension. The whole figure is saved, even for an axes. Other options are accepted and ignored.

exppdf.description: Exponential density with mean mu (default 1); note mu is the mean, not the rate.

exprnd.description: Exponential random numbers with mean mu.

extractAfter.description: Text after the first occurrence of pattern, or after character position pos. If the pattern does not occur the result is empty text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

extractBefore.description: Text before the first occurrence of pattern, or before character position pos. If the pattern does not occur the result is empty text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

extractBetween.description: Text between start and end markers (excluded unless 'Boundaries' is 'inclusive'), or between two character positions (both included). For a char vector every match is returned as a column cell array; for a cell array each element must contain exactly one match. Example: extractBetween('a[b]c[d]', '[', ']') is {'b'; 'd'}.

eye.description: Identity matrix: ones on the main diagonal, zeros elsewhere. A non-square size puts ones on the diagonal starting at the top-left. N-D sizes are not supported. Example: eye(2) is [1 0; 0 1].

ezcontour.description: Draws contour lines of f(x, y), a handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default. ezcontourf fills the areas between the lines.

ezcontourf.description: Draws contour lines of f(x, y), a handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default. ezcontourf fills the areas between the lines.

ezmesh.description: Like ezsurf, but draws a wireframe mesh.

ezplot.description: Plots a function given as a handle or as an expression in quotes over [-2*pi, 2*pi] or the given interval. A function of two variables, or an equation, is drawn as the curve where it is zero; two functions give the parametric curve (fx(t), fy(t)). Expressions in quotes need no dots before *, / and ^.

ezsurf.description: Draws the surface z = f(x, y) for a function handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default, and titles the plot with the expression. ezsurfc draws the same plot.

ezsurfc.description: Draws the surface z = f(x, y) for a function handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default, and titles the plot with the expression. ezsurfc draws the same plot.

factor.description: Row vector of the prime factors of the scalar n in ascending order, with repeats. Example: factor(12) is [2 2 3].

factorial.description: n! for each element of n, e.g. factorial(5) is 120. Returned as double.

false.description: Logical 0, or a logical array of zeros. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array.

fcdf.description: F distribution cumulative probability. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

fclose.description: Closes a file opened with fopen, or all of them. status is 0. An id that is not open is an error.

fcontour.description: Draws contour lines of f(x, y) over [-5, 5] in x and y, or over the given ranges.

feature.description: Reads an internal setting. 'numcores' gives the number of processor cores, 'getpid' the process number, 'DefaultCharacterSet' is 'UTF-8'. Other names return 0.

feof.description: True when there is nothing left to read from the file. Unlike some implementations this is already true right after the last byte has been read, without a further failed read.

ferror.description: Message of the most recent file error, such as a failed fseek, or '' when there was none (errnum is then 0). 'clear' resets it. mylab keeps one message for all files.

feval.description: Calls the function f, given as a handle or a name, with the remaining arguments. Example: feval('max', [3 8 1]) is 8.

fflush.description: Writes any buffered output of a file to disk. Accepted with any argument, including stdout, so that Octave-style code runs.

fft.description: Fast Fourier transform (discrete Fourier transform) along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim; each column of a matrix is transformed. n zero-pads or truncates to n points. The result is always complex; abs(Y) is the amplitude spectrum. Example: fft([1 0 0 0]) is [1 1 1 1].

fft2.description: Two-dimensional fast Fourier transform of a matrix, optionally padded or cropped to m-by-n.

fftn.description: N-dimensional discrete Fourier transform: the FFT along every dimension of X. siz pads or cuts X to that size first.

fftshift.description: Swaps the halves of a spectrum so the zero-frequency term sits in the middle, which suits plotting fft output against centred frequencies.

fgetl.description: Reads the next line of a file as text, without its line ending. Returns the number -1 at the end of the file, so test the result with ischar.

fgets.description: Reads the next line of a file as text, keeping its line ending; nchar limits how many characters are returned. Returns -1 at the end of the file.

fieldnames.description: Field names of a struct as a column cell array of char vectors, in creation order.

figure.description: Opens a new figure, or makes figure n (or figure handle f) current, creating it if needed. Later plots go to the current figure. f is a Figure handle with properties such as Number, Name, Color and Position, which may also be given as Name/Value options; other common window options (e.g. 'NumberTitle', 'Visible', 'Units') are accepted.

figurepalette.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

fileparts.description: Splits a file path into its folder, base name and extension (with the dot). Example: fileparts('a/b.txt') gives 'a', 'b' and '.txt'.

fileread.description: Entire contents of a text file (read as UTF-8) as one char vector.

filesep.description: Separator between folders in a path: '/' on Linux and macOS, '\' on Windows.

fill.description: Draws a filled polygon with corners (x(k), y(k)); c is a colour name or RGB triplet, and matrix x, y draw one polygon per column. fill replaces the plot unless hold is on; patch always adds to the current axes. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, DisplayName. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

fill3.description: Draws filled polygons in 3-D with corners (x(k), y(k), z(k)); matrix inputs draw one polygon per column. c is a colour name, an RGB triplet, or numbers mapped through the colormap. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth.

fillmissing.description: Replaces missing entries. Methods: 'constant' (the value v), 'previous', 'next', 'nearest' and, for numeric data, 'linear', 'spline', 'pchip' and 'makima'. Matrices are filled column by column (or along dim); tables variable by variable. Leading or trailing gaps are extrapolated by the interpolating methods unless 'EndValues' is 'none', 'nearest' or a constant. TF marks the entries that were filled. Example: fillmissing([1 NaN 3], 'linear') is [1 2 3].

filter.description: Applies the rational digital filter with numerator b and denominator a to the data x, along a row vector or down the columns of a matrix. Initial conditions are not supported. Example: filter(1, [1 -0.5], [1 1 1]) is [1 1.5 1.75].

filter2.description: Two-dimensional correlation of X with the kernel h in double precision. shape is 'same' (default), 'full' or 'valid'.

filtfilt.description: Zero-phase digital filtering: runs the filter forward and then backward, so the output has no phase delay and the filter's effect is squared. Works along a row vector or down columns. The data must be longer than three times the filter order.

fimplicit.description: Draws the curve where f(x, y) equals zero, over [-5, 5] in both directions by default. Example: fimplicit(@(x, y) x.^2 + y.^2 - 4)

find.description: Linear indices of the nonzero elements of x, in column-major order. n limits the result to the first (or 'last') n hits. With two or three outputs, returns row and column subscripts and the values. The result is a row for row-vector input, otherwise a column. Example: find([0 5 0 7]) is [2 4].

findall.description: Returns the graphics objects whose properties have the given values, searching all figures or only parent and the objects inside it. Several name/value pairs must all match; '-or' and '-not' combine conditions, '-regexp' matches text with a regular expression, '-property' tests that a property exists, and '-depth' limits how deep the search goes ('flat' is depth 0). The result is empty when nothing matches. findall does the same. Example: set(findobj(gca, 'Type', 'line'), 'LineWidth', 2)

findgroups.description: Numbers the groups formed by the unique values (or unique combinations of values) of the grouping vectors, in sorted order of those values. G gives the group number of each element (NaN when a value is missing); ID holds each group's value. Works for numeric, logical, cell arrays of text and string vectors, and for all variables of a table. Example: findgroups([5 3 5]) is [2 1 2].

findobj.description: Returns the graphics objects whose properties have the given values, searching all figures or only parent and the objects inside it. Several name/value pairs must all match; '-or' and '-not' combine conditions, '-regexp' matches text with a regular expression, '-property' tests that a property exists, and '-depth' limits how deep the search goes ('flat' is depth 0). The result is empty when nothing matches. findall does the same. Example: set(findobj(gca, 'Type', 'line'), 'LineWidth', 2)

findpeaks.description: Finds local maxima (peaks) of a vector: points higher than both neighbours, with a flat top reported at its first sample; the end points are never peaks. locs are indices, or positions from x (a scalar x is a sample rate). Options: MinPeakHeight, MinPeakProminence, MinPeakDistance, Threshold, SortStr ('ascend'/'descend') and NPeaks. Widths, prominences and plotting are not supported. Example: findpeaks([1 3 2 5 1]) is [3 5].

findprop.description: Describes a property of an object of a classdef class: a struct with Name, GetAccess, SetAccess, Dependent, Constant and more. Returns [] when there is no such property.

findstr.description: Starting positions where the shorter of the two texts occurs in the longer one. An old function; strfind is preferred.

fix.description: Rounds each element toward zero, dropping the fractional part. Example: fix(-2.7) is -2.

flintmax.description: 2^53, the largest value up to which every integer is exactly representable as a double. A class argument is not supported.

flip.description: Reverses the order of elements along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. Example: flip([1 2 3]) is [3 2 1].

flipdim.description: Old name of flip(A, dim): reverses the order of elements along dimension dim.

fliplr.description: Reverses the order of the columns (left-right mirror). Works on cell arrays too.

flipud.description: Reverses the order of the rows (up-down mirror). Works on cell arrays too.

floor.description: Rounds each element down, toward -Inf. Example: floor(-2.5) is -3.

fmesh.description: Like fsurf, but draws a wireframe mesh of z = f(x, y).

fminbnd.description: Minimizes a function of one variable on the interval [a, b] (golden section search with parabolic steps). output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

usage: x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon)
fmincon.description: Constrained nonlinear optimization: minimizes fun(x) from the start x0 subject to linear constraints, bounds and nonlinear constraints, where nonlcon returns [c, ceq] with c <= 0 and ceq = 0 required. Uses sequential quadratic programming with numerical gradients and finds a local minimum. Only the MaxIterations (or MaxIter) option is read. exitflag is 1 on success, -2 if the result is infeasible.

fminsearch.description: Minimizes a function of several variables without derivatives (Nelder-Mead simplex), starting at x0. Options TolX, TolFun, MaxIter and MaxFunEvals are read. output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output, grad, hessian] = fminunc(...)
fminunc.description: Minimizes a smooth function of several variables without constraints (quasi-Newton BFGS). grad is the gradient and hessian an approximation of the Hessian at the solution.

fopen.description: Opens a file and returns a file id (3 or higher) for the reading and writing functions, or -1 on failure with the reason in msg. permission is 'r' (read, the default), 'w' (create or empty, then write), 'a' (append), or 'r+', 'w+', 'a+' for reading and writing; a 'b' or 't' suffix is accepted and makes no difference, since line endings are never translated. machinefmt sets the default byte order for fread and fwrite: The byte order is 'l' or 'ieee-le' (little-endian), 'b' or 'ieee-be' (big-endian) or 'n' (native). encoding (default 'UTF-8') is used when text is read or written. A file opened for reading is also looked for on the search path. File ids 1 and 2 always mean the command window. Given a file id, fopen returns the file's name and settings; fopen('all') lists the open ids.

format.description: Chooses how many digits numbers display with: long shows about 15 significant digits, short (the default) about 5. 'compact' and 'loose' are accepted but change nothing.

fpdf.description: F distribution density with nu1 and nu2 degrees of freedom.

fplot.description: Plots the function handle f over the interval [a b] (default [-5 5]) by sampling it at many points; f is called with a vector and, if that fails, one point at a time. With two handles draws the parametric curve (fx(t), fy(t)).

fprintf.description: Formats data like sprintf and writes it out. Without a file id, or with fid 1 or 2, the text goes to the command window; otherwise to a file opened with fopen. No newline is added automatically. The optional output is the number of bytes written.

frame2im.description: Returns the image stored in a movie frame (its cdata), and the frame's colormap as a second output.

usage: A = fread(fid, size, precision, skip, machinefmt)
fread.description: Reads binary data from a file. size is the number of values, Inf (the default) for the rest of the file, or [m n] to fill an m-by-n matrix column by column (n may be Inf). precision says how the bytes are stored and what class is returned: 'uint8' (the default) reads bytes and returns double; 'int16=>int32' reads int16 and returns int32; '*int16' is short for 'int16=>int16'; 'uint8=>char' and '*char' return text. skip is a number of bytes to jump over after each value, or after each group of N values when the precision is written 'N*type'. count is the number of values actually read; a short read fills an incomplete last column with zeros. Precision names: 'uint8', 'int8', 'uint16', 'int16', 'uint32', 'int32', 'uint64', 'int64', 'single' ('float32'), 'double' ('float64'), 'char' and C-style names such as 'short', 'int', 'long', 'float' and 'uchar'. Bit-field precisions such as 'ubit3' are not supported. The byte order is 'l' or 'ieee-le' (little-endian), 'b' or 'ieee-be' (big-endian) or 'n' (native).

freqz.description: Frequency response of a digital filter at n points (default 512) from 0 up to the Nyquist frequency ('whole' goes around the full circle). w is in radians per sample, or f in Hz when the sample rate fs is given. A vector of frequencies may be given instead of n. No plot is drawn; plot abs(h) yourself.

frewind.description: Moves the position of a file back to its start.

frnd.description: Random numbers from the F distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. frnd(v1, v2, 3, 2) or frnd(v1, v2, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

fscanf.description: Reads formatted data from the rest of an open file, like sscanf: conversions such as %d, %f, %g and %s are applied repeatedly. size may be n, Inf or [m n] (with n possibly Inf) and fills the result column by column.

fseek.description: Moves the read/write position of a file by offset bytes from origin: 'bof' or -1 (start of file, the default), 'cof' or 0 (current position), 'eof' or 1 (end of file). Returns 0, or -1 (leaving the position unchanged) when the target lies outside the file.

fsolve.description: Solves the system of equations f(x) = 0, starting from x0. f returns a vector of residuals. Options are ignored.

fspecial.description: Ready-made filter kernels for imfilter. 'average' is a box of equal weights (3-by-3 by default); 'gaussian' a bell of size hsize (3) and standard deviation sigma (0.5); 'disk' a circular average of the given radius (5) with partly covered pixels weighted by area; 'laplacian' the 3-by-3 Laplacian with shape alpha (0.2); 'log' a Laplacian of Gaussian (5, 0.5); 'motion' a line of length len (9) at theta degrees (0) that imitates camera motion; 'sobel' and 'prewitt' emphasise horizontal edges (transpose for vertical); 'unsharp' sharpens. The 'motion' weights are an approximation and can differ in the last digits from other implementations.

usage: fsurf(fx, fy, fz, [umin umax vmin vmax])
fsurf.description: Draws the surface z = f(x, y) over [-5, 5] in x and y, or over the given ranges; three functions give a parametric surface. 'MeshDensity', n sets the number of grid points per direction.

ftell.description: Current position in a file, in bytes from its start.

full.description: Converts a sparse matrix to an ordinary full matrix. A full input is returned unchanged.

fullfile.description: Joins folder and file names with the operating system's separator. Example: fullfile('data', 'run1.csv') is 'data/run1.csv' on Linux.

func2str.description: Text form of a function handle: the function name, or the full expression starting with @ for an anonymous function.

fwrite.description: Writes the elements of A to a file as binary data, column by column. precision is the type stored in the file ('uint8' by default); values are rounded and clipped to its range. Text is written as character codes, or in the file's encoding with precision 'char'. skip leaves that many bytes untouched before each value. count is the number of elements written. With fid 1 or 2 the values are shown in the command window as characters. Precision names: 'uint8', 'int8', 'uint16', 'int16', 'uint32', 'int32', 'uint64', 'int64', 'single' ('float32'), 'double' ('float64'), 'char' and C-style names such as 'short', 'int', 'long', 'float' and 'uchar'. Bit-field precisions such as 'ubit3' are not supported. The byte order is 'l' or 'ieee-le' (little-endian), 'b' or 'ieee-be' (big-endian) or 'n' (native).

fzero.description: Finds a zero of a function of one variable, starting from x0 (a sign change is searched for around it) or inside the interval [a b] whose ends have opposite signs. output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

gamcdf.description: Gamma cumulative probability with shape a and scale b (default 1). Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

gamma.description: Gamma function of each element; gamma(n) equals factorial(n-1) for positive integers.

gammainc.description: Regularized incomplete gamma function: the lower tail P(a, x) by default, or the upper tail 1 - P with 'upper'. Note that x comes first. a must be non-negative.

gammaln.description: Natural log of the gamma function, useful when gamma itself would overflow.

gampdf.description: Gamma density with shape a and scale b (default 1).

gamrnd.description: Random numbers from the gamma (shape a, scale b) distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. gamrnd(a, b, 3, 2) or gamrnd(a, b, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

gca.description: Handle to the current axes, creating a figure and axes if needed. Its properties (XLim, YLim, Title, XLabel, FontSize, XScale, Box, XGrid, XTick, XTickLabel, ...) can be read and set with dot syntax or get/set, and most plotting functions accept it as their first input.

gcbf.description: The window that holds the component whose callback is running; empty outside callbacks.

gcbo.description: The component whose callback is running, and its window; empty outside callbacks.

gcd.description: Greatest common divisor of corresponding integer elements of a and b.

gcf.description: Handle to the current figure, creating one if none exists. f.Number is its figure number; the handle works with get, set, saveas, print and close.

gcp.description: The current parallel pool: a struct with NumWorkers 1, or [] with 'nocreate' because no pool is ever running.

genpath.description: The folder and all folders below it, joined with the path separator, for use with addpath. Folders named private or resources, and those whose names start with '@', '+' or '.', are left out. Returns '' if the folder does not exist.

geomean.description: Geometric mean: the n-th root of the product of n values. Negative values give NaN.

geornd.description: Random numbers from the geometric (failures before the first success) distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. geornd(p, 3, 2) or geornd(p, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

get.description: Reads a property of a graphics handle h (from gcf, gca, plot, title, ...). Property names ignore case. When h holds several handles (e.g. all lines returned by one plot call) the result is a cell array with one row per handle. get(h) returns a struct of the common properties. A figure number or 0 (the graphics root) also works as h. Dot syntax, e.g. h.LineWidth, reads the same properties.

getReport.description: Returns the text of an error caught with try/catch, including the function and line where it happened. 'basic' gives the message only. Example: try, f(); catch err, disp(getReport(err)), end

getString.description: Returns the text of a message object created with message.

getappdata.description: Returns the value stored on h under name by setappdata, or [] when there is none. With one input, returns everything stored on h as a struct.

getenv.description: Value of an operating-system environment variable, or '' if it is not set.

getfield.description: Value of a field, the same as s.name. Several names follow nested structs (s.a.b), and a cell array of subscripts indexes the value before it, so getfield(s, {2}, 'a', {3}) is s(2).a(3).

getframe.description: Captures the current axes (or the given axes or whole figure) as a movie frame: a struct with cdata, a height-by-width-by-3 uint8 image, and an empty colormap. rect = [left bottom width height] in pixels keeps part of the picture. Example: F(k) = getframe(gcf) inside a loop collects frames for movie or writeVideo.

getnhood.description: Neighbourhood of a structuring element as a logical matrix.

getpoints.description: Returns the points currently stored in the animated line h as row vectors.

getpref.description: Value of a stored preference. If it does not exist the default is stored and returned, or an error is raised when no default is given. With only a group, all its preferences are returned as a struct.

ginput.description: Reads n mouse clicks (or clicks until Enter) from the current figure window and returns their data coordinates as column vectors. It needs a live plot window; elsewhere it raises an error.

usage: x = gmres(A, b, restart, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
gmres.description: Solves A*x = b for a general square A with the generalized minimum residual method, restarted every `restart` iterations ([] for no restart). A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit.
