M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed. iter is [outer inner].

gobjects.description: Creates an array that holds graphics handles, to fill in a loop: h = gobjects(1, 3); h(k) = plot(...).

gpuArray.description: Returns A unchanged. mylab has no GPU arrays, so all calculations run on the CPU; this exists so that GPU-enabled code runs without edits.

gpuDevice.description: Describes the GPU in use. mylab has none, so the struct reports DeviceAvailable false and no memory; selecting or resetting a device does nothing.

gpuDeviceCount.description: Always 0: mylab does not use GPUs.

gradient.description: Numerical derivative: central differences in the interior and one-sided differences at the ends. Spacing may be a scalar step or a vector of coordinates. For a matrix, gx differentiates along each row (across columns) and gy along each column. Example: gradient([1 4 9 16]) is [3 4 6 7].

gray.description: n-by-3 colormap of greys from black to white (default 256 rows).

gray2ind.description: Converts a grayscale image to an indexed image with an n-level gray colormap (64 by default, 2 for a binary image).

graythresh.description: Threshold between 0 and 1 chosen by Otsu's method, which splits a 256-bin histogram into two groups with the smallest spread inside the groups. em (0..1) says how well the two groups separate.

grid.description: Shows or hides grid lines on the current axes; grid alone toggles.

usage: vq = griddata(x, y, v, xq, yq)
vq = griddata(x, y, v, xq, yq, method)
vq = griddata(x, y, z, v, xq, yq, zq)
griddata.description: Interpolates scattered samples v at (x, y) onto the query points, usually a grid from meshgrid. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'natural', 'cubic' and 'v4'. Query points outside the convex hull of the samples give NaN (except 'nearest' and 'v4'). 'natural' uses linear interpolation in mylab. Repeated sample points are averaged, with a warning.

groot.description: Handle to the graphics root, the parent of all figures (the same as handle 0). Its properties include CurrentFigure and ScreenSize.

groupsummary.description: Summary statistics for each group of table rows. The result has one row per group with the grouping values, a GroupCount column and one column per method and data variable, named like mean_Height. Methods: 'mean', 'sum', 'min', 'max', 'median', 'mode', 'std', 'var', 'range', 'numel', 'nnz', 'nummissing', 'all', or a function handle; NaN values are left out of the statistics. datavars defaults to all other numeric variables.

grp2idx.description: Turns a grouping variable into group numbers 1, 2, .... Numbers are grouped in sorted order, text in order of first appearance and categorical arrays in category order. names is a cell array of the group names. Missing values get NaN.

gtext.description: Places text where the mouse is clicked in a plot window. Without a live window the text is put in the middle of the axes and a warning suggests text(x, y, str).

guidata.description: Stores one value (usually a struct) with the window that h belongs to, or returns it. h can be the window or any component in it, so callbacks use it to share data: handles = guidata(hObject); handles.count = handles.count + 1; guidata(hObject, handles);

guide.description: Not available: GUIDE and its .fig files are not supported. Build the window in code with figure and uicontrol, or with uifigure.

guihandles.description: A struct with one field per Tag in the window of h; each field holds the component with that tag (several components when they share a tag). Tags that are not valid field names are skipped.

gunzip.description: Decompresses .gz files (or an http(s) address) next to the originals, or into outputfolder.

gzip.description: Compresses each file into a .gz file next to it, or in outputfolder. The originals are kept.

hamming.description: Hamming window of length n as a column vector.

hann.description: Hann (raised-cosine) window of length n as a column vector; the end points are zero.

hanning.description: Hann window variant without the zero end points, as a column vector.

harmmean.description: Harmonic mean: n divided by the sum of the reciprocals.

head.description: First k rows of a table or array (default 8).

height.description: Number of rows of a table (or of an array).

help.description: Shows the calling forms and a short description of a function. For functions and classdef classes in your own .m files it shows the comment block at the top of the file. With an output the text is returned instead of printed.

helpdlg.description: Prints the message with the label 'Help' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines.

hex2dec.description: Value of a hexadecimal digit string. A char matrix or cell array gives a column of numbers. Example: hex2dec('ff') is 255.

hgload.description: The .fig figure format is not supported; this raises an error. Save figures with saveas, print or exportgraphics as .png, .pdf or .svg instead.

hgsave.description: The .fig figure format is not supported; this raises an error. Save figures with saveas, print or exportgraphics as .png, .pdf or .svg instead.

hilb.description: n-by-n Hilbert matrix with entries 1/(i+j-1), a classic badly conditioned example.

hilbert.description: Analytic signal of real data: the real part is x and the imaginary part its Hilbert transform, so abs(z) is the instantaneous amplitude. Works along a row vector or down columns; any imaginary part of x is ignored.

hist.description: Older histogram function using equal-width bins (10 by default) or bins around the given centres. With outputs it returns the bin counts (and centres) without plotting; without outputs it draws the bars. Use histogram for a graphics handle.

histc.description: Counts values falling in each interval edges(k) <= x < edges(k+1); the last count is for values equal to the last edge. bin gives each value's interval (0 if outside). Older function; histcounts is usually more convenient.

histcounts.description: Counts how many values of x fall in each bin; every bin includes its left edge and the last bin also its right edge. Automatic bins use a round width (1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten) based on the spread of the data, with edges on multiples of it; integer data over a small range gets unit-width bins centred on the integers. Normalization may be 'count', 'probability', 'pdf', 'cdf', 'countdensity' or 'cumcount'. bin gives the bin number of each element (0 when outside). Example: histcounts(1:5) is [1 1 1 1 1] with edges 0.5:1:5.5.

histeq.description: Histogram equalization: remaps gray levels so that the output uses n levels (64 by default) about equally often, or so that its histogram resembles hgram. T is the mapping applied to the 256 input levels. Results can differ slightly from other implementations in how ties between output levels are resolved.

histogram.description: Plots a histogram of the finite values in x. Bins are chosen automatically (unit bins for small integer data) unless a bin count or edges are given, or the options NumBins, BinEdges, BinWidth, BinLimits or BinMethod ('integers'). Normalization may be 'count', 'probability', 'percentage', 'countdensity', 'pdf', 'cumcount' or 'cdf'. Style options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, DisplayName, Orientation. h is a Histogram handle: h.Values gives the bar heights, and changing h.NumBins, h.BinEdges, h.BinWidth or h.Normalization redraws the plot.

hms.description: Hour, minute and second of a datetime array, or the hours, minutes and seconds that make up each element of a duration array.

hold.description: With hold on (or hold all), new plots are added to the current axes instead of replacing them; hold off returns to replacing. hold alone toggles. An axes handle selects other axes. The axes property NextPlot ('add' or 'replace') shows the same state.

home.description: Clears the command window when the host program supports it; otherwise does nothing.

horzcat.description: Joins arrays side by side, the same as [A, B, ...]. They must have the same number of rows.

hot.description: n-by-3 colormap from black through red and yellow to white.

hour.description: Hour (0-23) of each element of a datetime array.

hours.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many hours. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of hours.

hsv.description: n-by-3 colormap cycling through the hues of the colour wheel.

hsv2rgb.description: Converts hue-saturation-value colours (each 0..1) to red-green-blue, as double.

hypot.description: sqrt(a.^2 + b.^2) element by element, computed without overflow for large values.

i.description: The imaginary unit, sqrt(-1). Can be overwritten by a variable named i; writing 1i is safer.

ichol.description: Incomplete Cholesky factor of a sparse symmetric positive definite matrix: a lower-triangular L with L*L' close to A, used to precondition pcg as pcg(A, b, tol, maxit, L, L'). By default L keeps the nonzero pattern of the lower triangle of A. opts.type = 'ict' with opts.droptol allows fill-in; opts.diagcomp adds a diagonal shift. An error is raised if a pivot is not positive.

idivide.description: Integer division with a chosen rounding: 'fix' (toward zero, the default), 'floor', 'ceil' or 'round'. At least one input must be an integer type (two integer inputs must share a class) and the result has that class. Example: idivide(int32(7), int32(2)) is 3.

ifft.description: Inverse fast Fourier transform. The result is returned as real when its imaginary parts are negligible; 'symmetric' always returns the real part.

ifft2.description: Two-dimensional inverse FFT; real output when the imaginary parts are negligible or with 'symmetric'.

ifftn.description: Inverse N-dimensional discrete Fourier transform. The result is real when its imaginary part is only round-off; 'symmetric' always returns the real part.

ifftshift.description: Undoes fftshift (they differ for odd lengths).

ilu.description: Incomplete LU factorization of a sparse square matrix, for use as a preconditioner: L*U approximates A while staying sparse. setup is a struct; setup.type is 'nofill' (default) or 'ilutp', and setup.droptol sets the drop tolerance for 'ilutp'.

im2bw.description: Binary image that is true where the brightness is above level, a fraction of the class range (default 0.5). RGB and indexed images are converted to grayscale first.

im2col.description: Rearranges m-by-n blocks of a matrix into columns. 'sliding' (default) takes every block position; 'distinct' takes non-overlapping blocks, padding the matrix with zeros.

im2double.description: Converts an image to double, rescaling integer classes to 0..1 (a uint8 255 becomes 1). double input is returned unchanged. With 'indexed' the values are colour numbers, which are only shifted to count from 1.

im2frame.description: Wraps an image in a movie frame struct with the fields cdata and colormap. RGB images given as doubles between 0 and 1 are stored as uint8; an indexed image keeps its colormap.

im2gray.description: Like rgb2gray, and a grayscale image is passed through unchanged.

im2int16.description: Converts an image to int16, rescaling so that the full range of the input class maps to -32768..32767.

im2single.description: Like im2double, but the result is of class single.

im2uint16.description: Converts an image to uint16, rescaling so that the full range of the input class maps to 0..65535.

im2uint8.description: Converts an image to uint8, rescaling as needed: 0..1 floating-point values map to 0..255 (values outside are clipped), uint16 values are divided by 257, and true becomes 255.

imabsdiff.description: Absolute difference of two images in their own class, without the underflow that X - Y would give for unsigned integers.

imadd.description: Adds two images, or a constant to an image, in the class of the image: integer results are rounded and clipped to the class range instead of wrapping.

imadjust.description: Stretches contrast: values from low_in to high_in are mapped to low_out..high_out (0..1 by default), with values outside clipped. Limits are fractions of the class range; [] means [0 1]. With no limits, the darkest and brightest 1% of pixels are saturated. gamma bends the mapping (below 1 brightens). For RGB images give limits, optionally one column per channel.

imag.description: Imaginary part of each element (0 for real input).

image.description: Shows the matrix C as an image, mapping its value range (or [cmin cmax]) onto the current colormap; row 1 is at the top. x and y give the centres of the first and last columns and rows. image and imshow behave the same way in mylab. Returns an Image handle (CData) on request.

imagesc.description: Shows the matrix C as an image, mapping its value range (or [cmin cmax]) onto the current colormap; row 1 is at the top. x and y give the centres of the first and last columns and rows. image and imshow behave the same way in mylab. Returns an Image handle (CData) on request.

imbinarize.description: Binary image from a grayscale image. With no threshold Otsu's method picks one for the whole image (see graythresh). T is a threshold between 0 and 1, or a matrix of them. 'adaptive' compares each pixel with the mean of its neighbourhood (about one eighth of the image size), which copes with uneven lighting: a pixel is false when it is clearly darker than its surroundings (15% at the default 'Sensitivity' of 0.5), so evenly lit areas come out true. Its results are close to, but not identical with, other implementations.

imbothat.description: The closing minus the image: keeps small dark details.

imclose.description: Closing, a dilation followed by an erosion: fills dark gaps and holes smaller than the structuring element.

imcomplement.description: Negative of an image: 255 - A for uint8, 1 - A for floating point, and logical NOT for a binary image.

imcrop.description: Cuts a rectangle out of an image. The rectangle is in pixel coordinates, so with whole numbers the result has height+1 rows and width+1 columns; a BoundingBox from regionprops gives exactly the region. Choosing the rectangle with the mouse is not supported.

imdilate.description: Dilation: each pixel becomes the largest value under the structuring element, which grows bright regions (and true regions of a binary image). The structuring element is a matrix of zeros and ones, such as the result of strel; its centre is element floor((size+1)/2).

imdivide.description: Divides images element by element, rounding and saturating integer classes.

imerode.description: Erosion: each pixel becomes the smallest value under the structuring element, which shrinks bright regions. The structuring element is a matrix of zeros and ones, such as the result of strel; its centre is element floor((size+1)/2).

imfill.description: Fills holes in a binary image (background regions that cannot be reached from the border), or flood-fills the background starting from the given linear indices or [row col] rows. Grayscale images and interactive use are not supported.

imfilter.description: Filters an image with the kernel h. By default this is correlation, the result has the size of A and pixels outside the image count as 0. padding may be a number, 'replicate' (repeat the border), 'symmetric' (mirror) or 'circular' (wrap around). 'conv' rotates the kernel by 180 degrees, 'full' returns the larger full result. The output has the class of A, so integer images are rounded and clipped; convert with im2double to keep fractions and negative values. A 2-D kernel is applied to each colour channel.

imfinfo.description: Describes an image file without loading the pixels: a struct with Filename, FileModDate, FileSize, Format, Width, Height, BitDepth, ColorType ('grayscale', 'truecolor' or 'indexed'), NumberOfFrames, DelayTime (hundredths of a second, GIF) and Colormap. A file with several frames gives one struct per frame.

imgaussfilt.description: Gaussian blur with standard deviation sigma (0.5 by default; [sy sx] for different amounts down and across). The kernel is 2*ceil(2*sigma)+1 wide unless 'FilterSize' is given, and the border is repeated unless 'Padding' says 'symmetric', 'circular' or a number.

imhist.description: Histogram of a grayscale image with n bins (256 by default, 2 for a binary image) spread over the range of the image's class. With outputs it returns the counts and bin centres as columns; with none it draws the histogram as a bar chart. For an indexed image the counts are per colormap entry.

immse.description: Mean squared error between two arrays of the same size, computed in double.

immultiply.description: Multiplies images element by element, saturating integer classes.

imnoise.description: Adds noise to an image. Mean and variance refer to a 0..1 intensity scale (defaults 0 and 0.01); density is the fraction of pixels set to black or white (0.05); speckle noise is multiplicative (0.05). Uses the generator controlled by rng.

imopen.description: Opening, an erosion followed by a dilation: removes bright details smaller than the structuring element while keeping larger shapes.

import.description: Lets later code call functions and classes of a +pkg folder without the package name: after import geom.* (or import geom.area), area(x) means geom.area(x). Unlike in MATLAB the import stays in effect for the rest of the session, in every function. Imports of packages that do not exist (Java packages, for example) are ignored.

importdata.description: Loads numeric text data. Without header lines the result is a matrix. With header lines it is a structure with data (the matrix), textdata (the header text) and, when the last header line names the columns, colheaders. The delimiter and number of header lines are detected when not given. .mat files are loaded as with load.

imread.description: Reads an image file (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, TIFF and the other formats Pillow knows) or an http(s) address. Grayscale images come back as an H-by-W array and colour images as H-by-W-by-3, of class uint8 (uint16 for 16-bit grayscale files, logical for 1-bit files). For an indexed file the first output holds zero-based uint8 colour numbers and map is the N-by-3 colormap; use ind2rgb to get colours. alpha is the transparency channel, or empty. A frame number (or 'Frames', k or 'all') picks frames of an animated GIF or multi-page TIFF; several frames are stacked along the fourth dimension. Files are also looked for on the search path. 16-bit RGB files are read with 8 bits per channel. The sample pictures that ship with MATLAB are not included.

imresize.description: Resizes an image by a scale factor or to a given size; one of rows and cols may be NaN to keep the aspect ratio. method is 'bicubic' (default), 'bilinear', 'nearest', 'box', 'lanczos2' or 'lanczos3'. When shrinking, the kernel is widened so that fine detail is averaged rather than aliased (not for 'nearest'; switch off with 'Antialiasing', false). The result has the class of A. Resizing an indexed image together with its colormap is not supported. Value ranges follow the class: 0..255 for uint8, 0..65535 for uint16, -32768..32767 for int16 and 0..1 for double and single.

imrotate.description: Rotates an image counter-clockwise by angle degrees about its centre. method is 'nearest' (default), 'bilinear' or 'bicubic'. The result is large enough to hold the whole rotated image ('loose') unless 'crop' keeps the original size; uncovered corners are 0. Multiples of 90 degrees are exact. 'bicubic' uses a cubic spline, so values differ slightly from other implementations.

imshow.description: Shows an image with square pixels and no axis ticks. Grayscale images use the gray colormap over the range of their class (0 to 255 for uint8, 0 to 1 for double; black and white for logical); [low high] sets the range and [] uses the image's own minimum and maximum. M-by-N-by-3 arrays are shown as colour, X with a colormap as an indexed image, and a file name is read first.

imsubtract.description: Subtracts images (or a constant) in the class of the image; unsigned results below 0 become 0.

imtophat.description: The image minus its opening: keeps small bright details.

imtranslate.description: Shifts an image tx pixels to the right and ty pixels down, keeping its size. Uncovered pixels are 0 or the fill value; fractional shifts are interpolated ('linear' by default, or 'nearest' or 'cubic').

imwrite.description: Writes an image to a file; the format comes from the extension or from fmt ('png', 'jpg', 'bmp', 'gif', 'tif', ...). uint8 data is written as is, double and single data is taken to span 0..1, logical data becomes a 1-bit image and 16-bit grayscale is kept in PNG and TIFF files. With a colormap the first input is an indexed image. 'Quality' (0-100, default 75) applies to JPEG and 'Alpha' adds transparency to a PNG. For GIF files 'WriteMode', 'append' adds a frame to an existing file, 'DelayTime' is the time each frame is shown in seconds, and 'LoopCount', Inf makes the animation repeat forever; a 4-D array writes several frames at once. Other options are accepted and ignored.

ind2gray.description: Grayscale image from an indexed image and its colormap.

ind2rgb.description: Turns an indexed image into a double RGB image by looking every colour number up in the colormap. Integer-class indices count from 0, double indices from 1.

ind2sub.description: Converts linear indices into subscripts for an array of size sz. With fewer outputs than dimensions, the last output counts through the remaining dimensions. Example: [r, c] = ind2sub([3 4], 8) gives r = 2, c = 3.

inf.description: Positive infinity; -Inf is negative infinity. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Example: 1/0 gives Inf.

inline.description: Creates a function from text, e.g. f = inline('x.^2 + 1'); f(3). Without argument names the variables in the expression are used in alphabetical order. The result is an anonymous function; new code should write @(x) x.^2 + 1.

innerjoin.description: Combines rows of two tables that have equal key values (by default all variables with the same name). Every matching pair of rows gives one output row; the result is sorted by key. Non-key variables of the right table are appended; names used in both tables get _left and _right suffixes. 'LeftVariables' and 'RightVariables' choose the variables to keep.

inpolygon.description: True for the query points (xq, yq) that lie inside or on the edge of the polygon with corners (xv, yv). on is true for points exactly on the edge. Separate several loops with NaN; a loop inside another makes a hole.

input.description: Shows prompt and reads a line from the user. The reply is evaluated as an expression, so typing 2*3 gives 6; an empty reply gives []. With 's' the raw text is returned instead.

inputParser.description: Creates an object that describes and checks the inputs of a function. Declare arguments with addRequired, addOptional and addParameter, then call parse(p, varargin{:}). Afterwards p.Results is a struct with one field per argument (fields in alphabetical order), p.UsingDefaults lists the arguments that were not given and p.Unmatched holds unknown name-value pairs when p.KeepUnmatched is true. Other settings: FunctionName (used in error messages), CaseSensitive (default false), PartialMatching (default true), StructExpand (default true). Example: p = inputParser; addRequired(p, 'n'); addParameter(p, 'Tol', 1e-3); parse(p, varargin{:}); p.Results

inputdlg.description: Asks for one line of text per prompt (prompts is text or a cell array) and returns the answers as a column cell array of character vectors; use str2double for numbers. An empty reply keeps that prompt's default. In a terminal or notebook the question is asked as text; when nobody can answer (for example in a batch run) the default is used and a note is printed. A front end that cancels returns {}.

inputname.description: Always returns ''. mylab does not record which variable names the caller used for a function's arguments, so code should fall back to its own default name.

insertAfter.description: Inserts new after every occurrence of pattern, or after character position pos. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

insertBefore.description: Inserts new before every occurrence of pattern, or before character position pos. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

int16.description: Converts to the int16 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -32768..32767, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int16(2.5) is 3.

int2str.description: Rounds x to integers and converts the result to text like num2str.

int32.description: Converts to the int32 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -2147483648..2147483647, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int32(2.5) is 3.

int64.description: Converts to the int64 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range about -9.2e18..9.2e18, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int64(2.5) is 3.

int8.description: Converts to the int8 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -128..127, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int8(2.5) is 3.

usage: q = integral(f, a, b, 'AbsTol', at, 'RelTol', rt)
integral.description: Numerical integral of f from a to b by adaptive quadrature; a and b may be Inf or -Inf. mylab calls f with one scalar at a time, so f need not be vectorized. Other options such as 'ArrayValued' or 'Waypoints' are not supported. Example: integral(@(x) x.^2, 0, 3) is 9.

usage: q = integral2(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
integral2.description: Numerical double integral of f(x, y) over xmin <= x <= xmax and ymin <= y <= ymax. ymin and ymax may be numbers or functions of x. f is called with scalars. Options are not supported.

integralImage.description: Summed-area table: J(r+1, c+1) is the sum of I(1:r, 1:c). The result is one row and one column larger than I, with zeros in its first row and column.

interp1.description: One-dimensional interpolation of the samples (x, y) at the points xq. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'previous', 'next', 'spline' (not-a-knot cubic spline), 'pchip' and 'cubic' (shape-preserving piecewise cubic) and 'makima' (modified Akima). Outside the range of x the result is NaN for the first four methods and extrapolated for the cubic ones, unless 'extrap' or a fill value is given. If y is a matrix, each column is interpolated. Example: interp1([1 2 3], [10 20 30], 2.5) is 25.

usage: Zq = interp2(X, Y, Z, Xq, Yq)
interp2.description: Interpolation on a 2-D grid. X and Y are grid vectors or meshgrid matrices (default 1:n and 1:m). A row vector Xq with a column vector Yq is expanded to a grid. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'cubic', 'spline' and 'makima'. Points outside the grid give NaN or extrapval. interp2(Z, k) refines the grid by halving the spacing k times (once if k is omitted).

usage: Vq = interp3(X, Y, Z, V, Xq, Yq, Zq)
interp3.description: Interpolates values on a 3-D grid made with meshgrid (X varies along the columns). Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'cubic', 'spline'. Points outside the grid give NaN, or extrapval.

interpft.description: Resamples periodic data to n points by zero-padding (or trimming) its Fourier transform.

usage: Vq = interpn(X1, X2, ..., V, Xq1, Xq2, ...)
interpn.description: Interpolates values on an N-dimensional grid made with ndgrid. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'cubic', 'spline'. Points outside the grid give NaN, or extrapval.

intersect.description: Values found in both a and b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given; c = a(ia) = b(ib). The result is a row unless a is a column. Accepts cell arrays of text. The 'rows' option is ignored. Example: intersect([3 1 2], [2 3 4]) is [2 3].

usage: x = intlinprog(f, intcon, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
intlinprog.description: Mixed-integer linear programming: like linprog, but the variables listed in intcon must take integer values. Pass [] for constraints that are not needed. Options are ignored.

intmax.description: Largest value an integer class can hold, returned in that class. Defaults to 'int32'. Example: intmax('uint8') is 255.

intmin.description: Smallest value an integer class can hold, returned in that class. Defaults to 'int32'. Example: intmin('int8') is -128.

inv.description: Inverse of a square matrix, so that A*Y is the identity. A warning is printed when A is singular or nearly so, and the result is then unreliable (possibly Inf). For solving A*x = b, A\b is faster and more accurate.

invhilb.description: The exact inverse of the n-by-n Hilbert matrix hilb(n). All its entries are integers.

ipermute.description: Undoes permute: ipermute(permute(A, order), order) gives back A.

iqr.description: Interquartile range: the 75th minus the 25th percentile, a spread measure robust to outliers.

isKey.description: True when the containers.Map m has the key. With a cell array of keys, returns a logical array. The same as m.isKey(key).

isMATLABReleaseOlderThan.description: True if the release mylab reports (R2023a) is older than the given one, e.g. isMATLABReleaseOlderThan('R2024a').

isStringScalar.description: True if x is a string array with exactly one element.

is_function_handle.description: True if x is a function handle such as @sin or @(t) t.^2.

isa.description: True if class(x) equals classname. Also accepts the group names 'numeric' (double, single or integer), 'float' (double or single) and 'integer' (any integer class). For objects of a classdef class it is also true for any superclass, e.g. isa(dog, 'Animal').

isappdata.description: True when setappdata stored something under name on h.

isbanded.description: True when A has no nonzeros beyond the given lower and upper bandwidths.

isbetween.description: True where lower <= t <= upper. The bounds may be datetimes or date text. intervalType is 'closed' (default), 'open', 'openleft' or 'openright'.

iscalendarduration.description: True when x is a calendar duration array.

iscategorical.description: True when x is a categorical array.

iscategory.description: True for each name that is a category of c.

iscell.description: True if x is a cell array.

iscellstr.description: True if C is a cell array in which every cell holds a char vector (or empty char).

ischar.description: True if x is a char array, e.g. text in single quotes.

iscolumn.description: True if A has exactly one column (a 0-by-1 array counts).

isdatetime.description: True when x is a datetime array.

isdeployed.description: Always false: mylab code never runs as a compiled standalone application.

isdiag.description: True if every entry of the numeric matrix A off the main diagonal is zero.

isdir.description: True if f names an existing folder.

isduration.description: True when x is a duration array.

isempty.description: True if A has no elements, i.e. at least one dimension is 0.

isenum.description: True when x is a member (or an array of members) of an enumeration class.

isequal.description: True if all inputs have the same size and contents. Numeric type is ignored, so isequal(1, int8(1)) is true. NaN is never equal to NaN; see isequaln.

isequaln.description: Like isequal, but NaN values in matching positions count as equal.

isfield.description: True if s is a struct with a field of that name; a cell array of names gives a logical array. Non-struct input gives false.

isfile.description: True if f names an existing file (not a folder).

isfinite.description: Logical array that is true where x is neither NaN nor infinite.

isfloat.description: True if x is a double or single array.

isfolder.description: True if f names an existing folder.

isgraphics.description: True for each element of h that is a valid (not deleted or closed) graphics handle, optionally of the given type such as 'line' or 'figure'. Figure numbers count as handles of open figures. ishandle and ishghandle are the same.

ishandle.description: Same as isgraphics: true for valid graphics handles.

ishermitian.description: True if the square matrix A equals its conjugate transpose A' ('skew': equals -A'). With tol, small differences relative to the size of A are allowed.

ishghandle.description: Same as isgraphics: true for valid graphics handles.

ishold.description: True if hold is on for the current axes.

isinf.description: Logical array that is true where x is Inf or -Inf.

isinteger.description: True if x has an integer class such as int8 or uint32. A double holding a whole number is not an integer type.

iskeyword.description: True if s is a reserved word of the language such as 'for' or 'end'. With no input, returns all keywords as a column cell array.

isletter.description: True for each alphabetic character in a char array; false for non-char input.

islogical.description: True if x is a logical (boolean) array.

ismatrix.description: True if A has exactly two dimensions (any size, including empty).

ismember.description: True where an element of a is found in s; loc gives the index of the first match in s (0 when absent). Works for numbers, text and cell arrays of text. With 'rows', each row of A is looked up among the rows of B and column vectors are returned. Example: ismember([1 2; 5 6], [5 6; 0 0], 'rows') is [false; true].

ismethod.description: True if obj has a public method called name.

ismissing.description: True where an element is missing: <missing> in a string array, NaN in a numeric array, or an empty char vector in a cell array. Returns a logical array the size of x.

isnan.description: Logical array that is true where x is NaN.

isnat.description: True where the elements of a datetime array are NaT.

isnumeric.description: True for double, single and integer arrays (real or complex). False for logical, char, cell, struct and string values.

isobject.description: True if x is an object: a containers.Map, a table, or an instance of a classdef class.

isordinal.description: True when the categories of c have an order (created with 'Ordinal', true).

isoutlier.description: Marks the outliers of A along its first non-singleton dimension. The default method 'median' flags values more than 3 scaled median absolute deviations from the median; 'mean' uses 3 standard deviations from the mean and 'quartiles' 1.5 interquartile ranges outside the quartiles.

ispref.description: True if the preference group, or the named preference in it, exists.

isprime.description: Logical array that is true where x is a prime number.

isprop.description: True if obj has a public property called name.

isreal.description: False only when x is stored as a complex array; a complex array whose imaginary parts are all zero still counts as not real. True for non-numeric values.

isrow.description: True if A has exactly one row (a 1-by-0 array counts).

issorted.description: True if the elements (or rows, with 'rows') are already in order. Other modes: 'strictascend', 'strictdescend' and 'strictmonotonic'. Works on cell arrays of text too.

isspace.description: True for each whitespace character in a char array; false for non-char input.

issparse.description: True when A is stored as a sparse matrix.

issquare.description: True if A has the same number of rows and columns.

isstr.description: Old name of ischar: true if x is a char array.

isstring.description: True if x is a string scalar, e.g. text in double quotes.

isstrprop.description: Tests each character of s for a category: 'alpha', 'digit', 'alphanum', 'wspace', 'upper', 'lower', 'punct' or 'cntrl'.

isstruct.description: True if x is a struct or struct array.

issymmetric.description: True if the square matrix A equals its transpose ('skew': equals minus its transpose). With tol, small differences relative to the size of A are allowed.

istable.description: True if x is a table.

istext.description: True if x is either a char array or a string.

istril.description: True if every entry above the main diagonal of the numeric matrix A is zero.

istriu.description: True if every entry below the main diagonal of the numeric matrix A is zero.

isundefined.description: True for the elements of a categorical array that have no category.

isunix.description: True when running on a POSIX system (Linux or macOS).

isvalid.description: True for a handle object (classdef handle class, containers.Map, ...) that has not been deleted with delete(h). For graphics handles it is false once the object has been deleted or its figure closed; for an array of graphics handles it returns one value per handle.

isvarname.description: True if s is a valid variable name: a letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, at most 63 characters, and not a keyword.

isvector.description: True if A is 1-by-n or n-by-1 with at least one element.

j.description: The imaginary unit, sqrt(-1). Can be overwritten by a variable named i; writing 1i is safer.

javachk.description: Returns a struct with a message saying that Java is not available in mylab.

jet.description: n-by-3 rainbow colormap (default 256 rows) from dark blue to dark red.

join.description: Text: joins the strings in C with a delimiter (default a space) along the last dimension, or along dim. Tables: adds to each row of Tleft the variables of the row of Tright with the same key values (by default the variables with the same name); every left row must match exactly one right row, and the left row order is kept.

jsondecode.description: Converts JSON text to a value. Objects become structs, arrays of numbers become column vectors or matrices (null becomes NaN), arrays of objects with the same fields become struct arrays, other arrays become cell arrays, true/false become logical values and a lone null becomes []. Field names that are not valid identifiers are changed (other characters become _). To read a file: jsondecode(fileread('data.json')).

jsonencode.description: Converts a value to JSON text. Structs and containers.Map become objects, vectors and cell arrays become arrays, matrices become arrays of rows, tables become an array with one object per row. NaN and Inf become null unless 'ConvertInfAndNaN' is false. 'PrettyPrint' adds line breaks and two-space indentation.

juliandate.description: Julian date (days since noon on November 24, 4714 BC in the proleptic Gregorian calendar), or the modified Julian date.

kaiser.description: Kaiser window of length n as a column; larger beta (default 0.5) gives lower side lobes.

keyboard.description: Pauses the program at this point and opens the K>> debugger prompt, where you can inspect variables, step (n, s) or continue (c). Only works in an interactive terminal; elsewhere it does nothing.

keys.description: Returns the keys of the containers.Map m as a cell array, in sorted order.

kmeans.description: k-means clustering of the rows of X into k groups. idx gives each row's cluster number, C the cluster centres, sumd the within-cluster sums of distances and D the distance from every point to every centre. Options: 'Distance' ('sqeuclidean' default or 'cityblock'), 'Replicates' (keep the best of several runs), 'MaxIter' (default 100) and 'Start' ('plus' k-means++ default, 'sample', 'uniform' or a k-by-p matrix). Rows with NaN get idx NaN. Results are random; set rng for repeatable runs.

knnsearch.description: For each row of Y, finds the nearest rows of X. idx(i, :) are the row numbers in X of the k nearest points (default k = 1), closest first, and D the distances. Distance names are the same as for pdist2.

kron.description: Kronecker product: every element A(i,j) is replaced by the block A(i,j)*B.

ksdensity.description: Kernel density estimate of the sample x: f is the estimated density at the points xi (100 points covering the data by default). Options: 'Bandwidth', 'Kernel' ('normal', 'box', 'triangle', 'epanechnikov'), 'Function' ('pdf', 'cdf', 'survivor'), 'NumPoints', 'Support' ('positive'), 'Weights'.

kurtosis.description: Sample kurtosis, a measure of how heavy the tails are; a normal distribution gives 3 (this is not the excess kurtosis). flag 0 applies the bias correction. NaN values are ignored.

label2rgb.description: Colours a label matrix for display: each label gets a colour from the colormap (a name such as 'jet', the default, or an N-by-3 matrix) and label 0 gets zerocolor (white by default; a letter such as 'k' or an RGB triple). 'shuffle' mixes the colour order. The result is uint8.

labelmatrix.description: Label matrix built from the struct returned by bwconncomp.

lasterr.description: Message (and identifier) of the most recent error. It is reliable inside a catch block; prefer 'catch err' and err.message in new code.

lasterror.description: Struct with the message, identifier and stack of the most recent error. It is reliable inside a catch block; prefer 'catch err' in new code.

lastwarn.description: Text of the most recent warning, or an empty char if there was none.

lcm.description: Least common multiple of corresponding integer elements of a and b.

ldivide.description: Same as A .\ B, i.e. B ./ A.

ldl.description: Block LDL factorization of a symmetric matrix: A = L*D*L' with D block diagonal (1-by-1 and 2-by-2 blocks). With three outputs L is lower triangular and P'*A*P = L*D*L'.

legend.description: Adds a legend naming the plotted items in drawing order, or only the graphics handles h. Without labels it uses each item's DisplayName, or data1, data2, ... legend off removes it, legend boxoff/boxon hides or shows its frame. Options: Location (a compass name such as 'northeast', 'southwest', 'best', or an outside position like 'eastoutside'), Orientation ('horizontal'), NumColumns, FontSize, Box, TextColor, Title. l is a Legend handle (String, Location, Box, FontSize, ...). With yyaxis, items from both sides are listed.

length.description: Size of the longest dimension of A, or 0 if A is empty. Example: length(ones(3, 7)) is 7.

license.description: Says whether a product is available: true for 'MATLAB' and for the toolboxes mylab covers in part ('image_toolbox', 'signal_toolbox', 'statistics_toolbox', 'optimization_toolbox'), false for everything else. mylab itself is free software under the MIT licence.

light.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. An output, if requested, is [].

lighting.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. Surfaces keep their flat colormap shading.

line.description: Draws a line in the current axes without clearing it, whatever the hold state. A matrix draws one line per column. Accepts the same Name/Value options as plot.

lines.description: n-by-3 matrix repeating the default line colour order (default 7 rows).

linkaxes.description: Gives the listed axes the same x and/or y limits (the range covering all of them) and keeps them in step when one of them changes. 'off' is accepted but does not unlink.

linkdata.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

linkprop.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab. Properties are not kept in sync.

usage: x = linprog(f, A, b, Aeq, beq)
x = linprog(f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
linprog.description: Linear programming: minimizes f'*x subject to A*x <= b, Aeq*x = beq and lb <= x <= ub, using the HiGHS solver. Pass [] for constraints that are not needed. exitflag is 1 when solved, 0 at the iteration limit, -2 when infeasible and -3 when unbounded (then x is []). An options argument is ignored.

linsolve.description: Solves the linear system A*x = b, the same as A\b. An options struct is not supported.

linspace.description: Row vector of n points evenly spaced from a to b, both ends included. n defaults to 100. Example: linspace(0, 1, 5) is [0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1].

listdlg.description: Lets the user choose from a numbered list and returns the chosen item numbers and ok = 1, or [] and ok = 0 after a cancel. The default selection is InitialValue (item 1). In a terminal or notebook the question is asked as text; when nobody can answer (for example in a batch run) the default is used and a note is printed.

listener.description: Like addlistener: calls callback(source, eventData) when obj fires the event. Keep L; delete(L) stops listening.

load.description: Reads variables from a .mat file into the workspace, or into the fields of S when an output is given. Numeric data is loaded as double. A .csv, .txt or .dat file is read as a numeric matrix and stored in a variable named after the file (or returned).

log.description: Natural logarithm of each element. log(0) is -Inf and negative inputs give complex results.

log10.description: Base-10 logarithm of each element; negative inputs give complex results.

log1p.description: log(1 + x) computed accurately when x is tiny. Inputs below -1 give NaN.

log2.description: Base-2 logarithm of each element; negative inputs give complex results. The two-output form [f, e] = log2(x) is not supported.

logical.description: Converts to logical: nonzero becomes true, zero becomes false. NaN input is an error.

loglog.description: Like plot, but with logarithmic x and y axes.

logm.description: Matrix logarithm, the inverse of expm. May be complex.

lognrnd.description: Random numbers from the lognormal distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. lognrnd(mu, sigma, 3, 2) or lognrnd(mu, sigma, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

logspace.description: Row vector of n points spaced evenly on a log scale from 10^a to 10^b. n defaults to 50. Example: logspace(0, 2, 3) is [1 10 100].

lower.description: Converts text to lower case, character by character, so the length never changes. Works on char arrays, strings, string arrays and cells.

ls.description: Lists the files in a folder, or those matching a wildcard pattern. With an output the names are returned as the rows of a char matrix, padded with spaces (on every platform).

usage: x = lsqcurvefit(fun, x0, xdata, ydata, lb, ub)
lsqcurvefit.description: Nonlinear curve fitting by least squares: finds parameters x so that fun(x, xdata) matches ydata as closely as possible, starting from x0. Uses Levenberg-Marquardt, or a trust-region method when bounds are given. Options StepTolerance (TolX) and FunctionTolerance (TolFun) are read. Example: lsqcurvefit(@(p, t) p(1)*exp(p(2)*t), [1 -1], t, y).

usage: x = lsqnonlin(fun, x0, lb, ub, options)
lsqnonlin.description: Nonlinear least squares: minimizes the sum of squares of the residual vector returned by fun(x), starting from x0, optionally within bounds. Methods and options as in lsqcurvefit.

lsqnonneg.description: Non-negative least squares: minimizes norm(C*x - d) subject to x >= 0. resnorm is the squared residual norm.

lsqr.description: Least-squares solution of A*x = b for a rectangular or square matrix, by an iterative method that only needs products with A and A'. tol defaults to 1e-6.

lu.description: LU factorization with partial pivoting. With three outputs, P*A = L*U where L is unit lower triangular. With two outputs, L already includes the row permutation, so A = L*U.

mad.description: Mean absolute deviation from the mean (flag 0, default) or median absolute deviation from the median (flag 1). NaN values are ignored.

mag2db.description: Converts amplitude ratio to decibels: 20*log10(m). Negative values give NaN.

magic.description: n-by-n magic square: every row, column and both main diagonals add up to the same value, n*(n^2+1)/2. Each integer 1..n^2 appears once. magic(2) is returned as [4 3; 1 2] even though no true 2-by-2 magic square exists.

makima.description: Modified Akima piecewise cubic interpolation, which avoids most overshoot without flattening the curve as much as pchip. Returns values at xq or a piecewise polynomial.

mat2cell.description: Cuts a 2-D array into blocks and returns them in a cell array. r lists the block heights and c the block widths; they must add up to the size of A (c defaults to all columns). Example: mat2cell(magic(4), [2 2], [3 1]) gives a 2-by-2 cell.

mat2gray.description: Rescales a matrix to a double image between 0 and 1: low maps to 0 and high to 1, with values outside clipped. Without limits the smallest and largest elements are used.

mat2str.description: Text that rebuilds the matrix A when evaluated, with n significant digits (15 by default). With 'class' the text is wrapped in the class name, e.g. int8([1 2 3]). An empty array is written as zeros(m,n).

material.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

matlabpool.description: Accepted for old code and does nothing; the pool size is 0.

max.description: Largest element along the first dimension whose size is not 1 (or along dim, or over 'all'). idx gives the position of the first maximum. NaN values are skipped unless every value is NaN; complex values are compared by magnitude. max(A, B) takes the larger of A and B element by element. Example: [m, i] = max([3 9 2]) gives m = 9, i = 2.

maxk.description: The k largest elements along the first non-singleton dimension (or dim), largest first. NaN values come last. I gives their indices. Example: maxk([3 9 4 7], 2) is [9 7].

mean.description: Arithmetic average, along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. 'omitnan' ignores NaN values. The result is double, also for integer input; mean([]) is NaN. Example: mean([1 2; 3 4]) is [2 3].

mean2.description: Mean of all elements of an array, as double.

medfilt1.description: One-dimensional median filter of order n (default 3): each output is the median of a window around the sample, which removes spikes while keeping edges. padding is 'zeropad' (default) or 'truncate'; 'omitnan' ignores NaN.

medfilt2.description: Median filter: each pixel becomes the median of its m-by-n neighbourhood (3-by-3 by default), which removes salt-and-pepper noise. Outside the image is 0 unless 'symmetric' mirrors the border. Colour images are filtered one channel at a time.

median.description: Middle value after sorting (the average of the two middle values for an even count), along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. Any NaN makes the result NaN unless 'omitnan' is given.

memory.description: Rough memory figures: user has MaxPossibleArrayBytes, MemAvailableAllArrays and MemUsedMATLAB; sys.PhysicalMemory has Available and Total. Values are 0 where the platform does not report them.

menu.description: Shows numbered choices and returns the number picked, or 0 if no valid choice was made. When nobody can answer, the first choice is used.

mergecats.description: Combines several categories into one, named newname (or the first of oldnames).

mesh.description: Draws a 3-D wireframe surface in the current axes, replacing it unless hold is on. meshc currently draws the same plot without contour lines. Returns a Surface handle on request.

meshc.description: Draws a 3-D wireframe surface in the current axes, replacing it unless hold is on. meshc currently draws the same plot without contour lines. Returns a Surface handle on request.

meshgrid.description: Builds grid coordinates from vectors: each row of X is a copy of x and each column of Y is a copy of y, so X and Y are numel(y)-by-numel(x). Handy for evaluating a function of two variables over a grid. With three vectors it builds 3-D grids.

message.description: Creates a message object from a message identifier such as 'MyPkg:myId'. mylab has no message catalog, so getString(msg) returns the identifier followed by the arguments. error(message(id)) raises an error with that identifier.

methods.description: Lists the public methods of an object or class; with an output, returns them as a cell column.

mex.description: Raises an error: compiled MEX files cannot be built or run by mylab. Projects usually ship a plain .m version of such functions, which works.

mfilename.description: Name of the .m file that is currently running, without folder or extension. 'fullpath' adds the folder, 'fullpathext' the folder and extension. Empty when called from the prompt.

milliseconds.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many milliseconds. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of milliseconds.

min.description: Smallest element along the first dimension whose size is not 1 (or along dim, or over 'all'). idx gives the position of the first minimum. NaN values are skipped unless every value is NaN. min(A, B) takes the smaller of A and B element by element.

mink.description: The k smallest elements along the first non-singleton dimension (or dim), smallest first. NaN values come last. Example: mink([3 9 4 7], 2) is [3 4].

usage: x = minres(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
minres.description: Solves A*x = b for a symmetric (possibly indefinite) A with the minimum residual method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed.

minute.description: Minute (0-59) of each element of a datetime array.

minutes.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many minutes. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of minutes.

missing.description: A missing value. Here it is a string scalar holding <missing>; ismissing(m) is true.

mkdir.description: Creates a folder, including any missing parent folders. It is not an error if the folder already exists. The optional output is true.

mkpp.description: Builds a piecewise polynomial. Row k of coefs holds the coefficients of piece k (highest power first) in the local variable x - breaks(k); d is the number of components for a vector-valued polynomial. Example: ppval(mkpp([0 1 2], [1 0; -1 1]), 1.5) is 0.5.

mldivide.description: Same as A \ B, which solves A*X = B (least squares if A is not square).

mod.description: Remainder after division, defined as a - floor(a./b).*b, so a nonzero result has the sign of b. mod(a, 0) is a. Example: mod(-1, 3) is 2. See rem for the truncating version.

mode.description: Most frequent value, along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given. Ties go to the smallest value and NaN is ignored. Only the first output is supported.

month.description: Month numbers (1-12) of a datetime array, or the month names as a cell array of text. Serial date numbers and date text are also accepted.

more.description: Accepted for compatibility; output is never paged, so it does nothing.

movefile.description: Moves or renames a file or folder. source may contain wildcards, and destination may be an existing folder to move into. With outputs, [status, message, messageId] report success (true) or the reason for failure instead of raising an error.

movegui.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

movevars.description: Moves table variables to a new position, before or after another variable (given by name or number), or to the end.

movie.description: Plays the frames in F (from getframe or im2frame) n times at fps frames per second in a plot window. Without a live window it returns at once: the frames were already recorded as an animation while they were drawn.

movmax.description: Moving maximum over a sliding window; options as in movmean.

movmean.description: Moving (rolling, sliding-window) average over windows of k samples centred on each point (for even k, one more sample before than after), or kb before and kf after. Near the ends the window shrinks by default; 'Endpoints' can be 'discard', 'fill' (NaN) or a number. SamplePoints are not supported. Example: movmean([1 2 3 4 5], 3) is [1.5 2 3 4 4.5].

movmedian.description: Moving median over a sliding window, useful for removing spikes; options as in movmean.

movmin.description: Moving minimum over a sliding window; options as in movmean.

movstd.description: Moving standard deviation over a sliding window; w = 1 normalizes by the window size instead of size-1. Other options as in movmean.

movsum.description: Moving sum over a sliding window; windows and options work as in movmean.

movvar.description: Moving variance over a sliding window; options as in movstd.

mrdivide.description: Same as B / A, which solves X*A = B.

msgbox.description: Prints the message with the label 'Message' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines. icon 'error', 'warn' or 'help' changes the label.

mustBeA.description: Validation function: raises an error unless value is of one of the named classes (a class name, or a cell/string array of names; subclasses count).

mustBeFile.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value names an existing file, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFile}.

mustBeFinite.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is Inf or NaN, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFinite}.

mustBeFolder.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value names an existing folder, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFolder}.

mustBeGreaterThan.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is greater than c.

mustBeGreaterThanOrEqual.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is at least c.

mustBeInRange.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element lies between lower and upper (inclusive).

mustBeInteger.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is a finite whole number, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeInteger}.

mustBeLessThan.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is less than c.

mustBeLessThanOrEqual.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is at most c.

mustBeMember.description: Validation function: raises an error unless value (number, text or cell of text) is one of the allowed values.

mustBeNegative.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is less than zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNegative}.

mustBeNonNan.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is NaN, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonNan}.

mustBeNonempty.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is not empty, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonempty}.

mustBeNonnegative.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is zero or greater, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonnegative}.

mustBeNonpositive.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is zero or less, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonpositive}.

mustBeNonzero.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonzero}.

mustBeNonzeroLengthText.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is text with at least one character, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonzeroLengthText}.

mustBeNumeric.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a numeric array, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNumeric}.

mustBeNumericOrLogical.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is numeric or logical, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNumericOrLogical}.

mustBePositive.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is greater than zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBePositive}.

mustBeReal.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value has no imaginary part, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeReal}.

mustBeText.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a char vector, string, or cell array of char vectors, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeText}.

mustBeTextScalar.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is one piece of text (char row vector or string scalar), and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeTextScalar}.

mustBeVector.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a row or column vector, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeVector}.

mvnpdf.description: Density of the multivariate normal distribution at each row of X. mu defaults to zero and Sigma to the identity matrix.

mvnrnd.description: Random vectors from the multivariate normal distribution with mean mu (a row) and covariance matrix Sigma; one sample per row of R.

nan.description: Not-a-Number, the result of undefined operations such as 0/0. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. NaN is unequal to everything, itself included; test for it with isnan.

nanmax.description: Maximum that ignores NaN values, like max.

nanmean.description: Mean that ignores NaN values; same as mean(..., 'omitnan').

nanmin.description: Minimum that ignores NaN values, like min.

nanstd.description: Standard deviation that ignores NaN values; flag 1 normalizes by N instead of N-1.

nansum.description: Sum that ignores NaN values; same as sum(..., 'omitnan').

nargchk.description: Returns an error message if n is outside low..high, or an empty value when it is in range; typically used as error(nargchk(1, 3, nargin)). With 'struct' the result is a struct with message and identifier. narginchk is the modern replacement.

nargin.description: Inside a function, the number of inputs the caller passed. nargin(fun), with a function name or handle, is the number of inputs fun declares; it is negative when the list ends in varargin (-3 for f(a, b, varargin)).

narginchk.description: Inside a function, throws an error if the number of inputs passed is below minargs or above maxargs.

nargout.description: Inside a function, the number of outputs the caller asked for. nargout(fun), with a function name or handle, is the number of outputs fun declares; it is negative when the list ends in varargout, and -1 for an anonymous function.

nargoutchk.description: Accepted for compatibility; mylab does not check anything.

native2unicode.description: Converts bytes in the given character encoding (default UTF-8) to text.

nbinrnd.description: Random numbers from the negative binomial distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. nbinrnd(r, p, 3, 2) or nbinrnd(r, p, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

nchoosek.description: With scalar n, the number of ways to pick k items from n (the binomial coefficient). With a vector v, every k-element combination of its entries, one per row. Example: nchoosek(5, 2) is 10.

ndgrid.description: Like meshgrid but the first vector runs along dimension 1 (down the rows), the second along dimension 2 and so on: X and Y are numel(x)-by-numel(y).

ndims.description: Number of dimensions of A, never less than 2. Example: ndims(zeros(2, 3, 4)) is 3.

newline.description: A char vector holding the line-feed character (code 10).

nextpow2.description: Smallest integer p with 2^p >= abs(n), element by element; handy for choosing an FFT length. Example: nextpow2(100) is 7.

nexttile.description: Creates the next axes of the current tiled layout and makes it current; nexttile(k) goes to tile k (counting along rows) and [r c] makes an axes spanning r rows and c columns. Without a layout a 'flow' layout is started.

nnz.description: Number of nonzero elements in x.

nonzeros.description: Column vector of the nonzero elements of A, in column-major order.

norm.description: For a vector, the p-norm (sum(abs(v).^p))^(1/p); p defaults to 2, the Euclidean length, and Inf or -Inf give the largest or smallest magnitude. For a matrix, p may be 1, 2 (default, the largest singular value), Inf or 'fro' (Frobenius). Example: norm([3 4]) is 5.

normalize.description: Rescales data along the first dimension whose size is not 1. method is 'zscore' (default; option 'std' or 'robust'), 'range' (to [0 1] or a given [a b]), 'norm' (divide by the p-norm, default 2), 'center' (subtract the mean, the median or a value) or 'scale' (divide by the std, 'mad', 'first', 'iqr' or a value).

normcdf.description: Normal cumulative distribution function: the probability that a value is at most x. Defaults mu = 0, sigma = 1. 'upper' gives the accurate upper tail. Example: normcdf(0) is 0.5.

normest.description: Estimate of the 2-norm (largest singular value) of a matrix without converting it to full form.

norminv.description: Inverse of normcdf (normal quantile). Example: norminv(0.975) is about 1.96.

normpdf.description: Normal (Gaussian) probability density at x, with mean mu (default 0) and standard deviation sigma (default 1). Inputs expand against scalars. sigma <= 0 gives NaN.

normrnd.description: Normally distributed random numbers with the given mean and standard deviation, shaped like the parameters or by the size arguments. Uses the generator controlled by rng.

notify.description: Fires an event of the handle object obj: every listener added with addlistener is called as callback(obj, eventData). The event must be declared in an events block of the class. Without eventData the callback gets an object with the properties Source and EventName.

now.description: The current local date and time as a serial date number. A serial date number counts days from year 0, with the time of day as the fraction.

nthargout.description: Calls f with the given inputs and returns only its n-th output. A vector n returns several outputs as a cell array; nout sets how many outputs f is asked for. Example: nthargout(2, @max, [3 9 2]) is 2.

nthroot.description: Real n-th root of each element; for negative x with odd n the real negative root is returned, e.g. nthroot(-8, 3) is -2. Negative x with an even or non-integer n is an error.

null.description: Orthonormal basis for the null space of A: the columns of Z satisfy A*Z = 0.

num2cell.description: Cell array with each element of A in its own cell. With dims, the listed dimensions are kept together: num2cell(A, 1) puts each column of A in one cell.

num2str.description: Converts numbers to text. Integers print in full; other values keep four digits after the decimal point (at least five significant digits for small values), with trailing zeros dropped. precision sets the number of significant digits and format is a sprintf format. Matrices give a char matrix with one row per row. Text input is returned as is. Example: num2str(pi) is '3.1416'.

numel.description: Total number of elements in A, the product of all its dimensions.

numfields.description: Number of fields of the struct s (0 if s is not a struct).

nzmax.description: Amount of storage allocated for nonzeros: nnz(S) (at least 1) for a sparse matrix and numel(A) for a full one.

ode113.description: Solver for non-stiff problems at tight tolerances. mylab uses a high-order (8th order) Runge-Kutta method instead of a multistep method; options and outputs are as for ode45.

ode15s.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

ode23.description: Like ode45 but with a lower-order (2,3) Runge-Kutta pair, which can be cheaper at loose tolerances. Supports the same options and outputs.

ode23s.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

ode23t.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

ode23tb.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

usage: [t, y, te, ye, ie] = ode45(f, tspan, y0, options)
ode45.description: Solves the ODE y' = f(t, y) from y(tspan(1)) = y0 with an explicit Runge-Kutta (4,5) pair. If tspan has two elements, the output holds the solver steps, refined with four points per step taken from the solver's own interpolant; with more elements, the solution at exactly those times. Options from odeset: RelTol (default 1e-3), AbsTol (1e-6), MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine and Events. An event function [value, isterminal, direction] = g(t, y) reports zero crossings of value (direction 1: rising only, -1: falling only, 0: both); te, ye and ie give their times, states and indices, and a terminal event stops the integration. sol is a structure with x, y (and xe, ye, ie) for use with deval.

ode78.description: High-order Runge-Kutta solver for smooth non-stiff problems at tight tolerances. Options and outputs are as for ode45.

ode89.description: High-order Runge-Kutta solver (the same method as ode78 here). Options and outputs are as for ode45.

odeget.description: Reads one option from an odeset structure (the name is not case sensitive), or returns default (or []) when it is not set.

odeset.description: Creates or updates an options structure for the ODE solvers, e.g. odeset('RelTol', 1e-6, 'Events', @myevents).

onCleanup.description: Runs the given function (no inputs) when the variable c goes away: when the function that created it returns or stops with an error, or when c is cleared. Typical use: fid = fopen(name); c = onCleanup(@() fclose(fid)); The function does not run when c is merely overwritten, and objects stored inside cells or structs are not tracked. An error inside the cleanup function is reported as a warning.

ones.description: Array filled with 1. With no size it returns the scalar 1; n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. A class name sets the type.

open.description: open(v) starts a VideoWriter file so that writeVideo can add frames. open(filename) loads a .mat file; other files are not opened because mylab has no editor windows, and .fig files are not supported.

openfig.description: The .fig figure format is not supported; this raises an error. Save figures with saveas, print or exportgraphics as .png, .pdf or .svg instead.

optimoptions.description: Same as optimset; the solver name is accepted and ignored. Returns a plain struct.

optimset.description: Builds an options struct from name/value pairs for fzero, fminsearch and similar solvers. mylab reads TolX, TolFun, MaxIter and MaxFunEvals where they apply and ignores other names.

or.description: Same as A | B (element-wise logical OR).

orderfields.description: Reorders the fields of a struct: alphabetically, in the order of a cell array of names, by a permutation vector, or like the fields of another struct. p is the permutation that was applied.

ordfilt2.description: Order-statistic filter: each pixel becomes the order-th smallest value among the neighbours marked by the nonzero elements of domain. order 1 is a minimum filter.

orth.description: Orthonormal basis for the column space (range) of A.

otsuthresh.description: Otsu's threshold computed from histogram counts; level is the chosen bin as a fraction of the bin range.

outerjoin.description: Like innerjoin but also keeps rows without a match ('Type' 'full', 'left' or 'right'), filling the missing side with NaN, empty text or <missing>. Without 'MergeKeys' the key variables of both tables are kept (with _left and _right suffixes); with it they are merged into one.

pad.description: Pads text with spaces (or the single character ch) to length n. side is 'right' (default), 'left' or 'both'. Without n, the elements of a cell or string array are padded to the length of the longest one. Text already longer than n is left alone. Example: pad('ab', 5, 'left', '*') is '***ab'.

padarray.description: Enlarges an array by padsize(k) elements along dimension k. The new elements are 0, padval, or come from the array itself: 'replicate' repeats the border, 'symmetric' mirrors it and 'circular' wraps around. direction is 'both' (default), 'pre' or 'post'.

pagemtimes.description: Matrix multiplication applied page by page: each 2-D slice X(:,:,k) is multiplied by the matching slice Y(:,:,k). The inner dimensions of each pair of pages must agree.

pan.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

parpool.description: Accepted for compatibility. mylab runs code in a single process, so no workers are started; the returned struct describes a pool with NumWorkers 1, and delete(pool) does nothing.

parse.description: Checks the given arguments against the declarations of the inputParser p and fills p.Results, p.Unmatched and p.UsingDefaults. Raises an error that names the argument when a required argument is missing, a validator rejects a value or a parameter name is unknown. Example: p = inputParser; addRequired(p, 'n'); addParameter(p, 'Tol', 1e-3); parse(p, varargin{:}); p.Results

parula.description: n-by-3 matrix of RGB colours (default 256) running from dark blue through green to yellow. mylab uses matplotlib's perceptually uniform 'viridis' map for parula, also the default colormap. Use with colormap, e.g. colormap(parula(16)).

pascal.description: Pascal matrix: P(i, j) is the binomial coefficient (i+j-2 choose j-1), a symmetric positive definite matrix of integers. pascal(n, 1) is a lower-triangular factor with alternating column signs that is its own inverse.

patch.description: Adds filled polygons to the current axes without clearing them. Polygons are given by corner coordinates, or by a vertex list V (one row per point, 2 or 3 columns) and a face list F whose rows hold vertex numbers. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, FaceVertexCData (one number or RGB row per face).

path.description: Current search path as one char vector with folders separated by the system path separator.

pathsep.description: The character that separates folders in a search path: ':' (';' on Windows).

pause.description: Waits n seconds (at most an hour). pause with no argument, or with text such as 'on', returns immediately instead of waiting for a key press. With a figure open it also refreshes the plot; where there is no live window it records an animation frame like drawnow and waits only briefly.

pbaspect.description: Sets the relative lengths of the sides of the plot box; pbaspect([1 1 1]) makes it square and pbaspect([2 1 1]) twice as wide as high.

usage: [coeff, score, latent, tsquared, explained, mu] = pca(X)
pca.description: Principal component analysis of the data in X (one observation per row, one variable per column). The columns of coeff are the principal directions, score the data in those coordinates, latent the variance along each, explained the percentage of the total variance and mu the column means. Rows with NaN are skipped. The sign of each direction is chosen so that its largest element is positive. 'Centered', false skips subtracting the means.

usage: x = pcg(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
pcg.description: Solves A*x = b for a symmetric positive definite A with the preconditioned conjugate gradient method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed. maxit defaults to min(n, 20).

pchip.description: Shape-preserving piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation: no overshoot between data points, and monotone data stay monotone. Returns values at xq or a piecewise polynomial for ppval.

pcolor.description: Draws the matrix C as a flat grid of coloured cells. Each cell takes the colour of its lower-left corner, so the last row and column of C are not shown; shading interp blends the colours. The y-axis points up (unlike imagesc).

pdist.description: Pairwise distances between the rows of X, returned as a row vector (use squareform to get a matrix). metric: 'euclidean' (default), 'squaredeuclidean', 'seuclidean', 'cityblock', 'chebychev', 'minkowski', 'cosine', 'correlation', 'spearman', 'hamming' or 'jaccard'.

pdist2.description: Distances between each row of X and each row of Y: D(i, j) is the distance from X(i, :) to Y(j, :). distance is 'euclidean' (default), 'squaredeuclidean', 'cityblock', 'chebychev', 'minkowski' (with the exponent as next argument), 'cosine', 'correlation', 'hamming', 'jaccard', 'seuclidean', 'spearman' or 'mahalanobis'. With 'Smallest' or 'Largest', k, each column holds the k nearest (or farthest) distances for one row of Y, and I the row numbers in X.
