With an output it returns a struct array with fields Name, Version, Release and Date for MATLAB and for the toolboxes mylab covers in part (Image Processing, Signal Processing, Statistics and Machine Learning, Optimization); ver('signal') selects one, and an unknown product gives an empty struct array.

verLessThan.description: True if the installed version of a product is older than the given version text, e.g. verLessThan('matlab', '9.4'). mylab compares against the versions listed by ver (MATLAB 9.14 and the matching 'images', 'signal', 'stats' and 'optim' versions). Any other toolbox is not available and counts as older than every version, so the result is true rather than an error.

version.description: Version text. So that programs checking for a recent MATLAB take their modern code path, mylab answers as MATLAB 9.14 (R2023a): version returns '9.14.0 (R2023a) mylab x.y.z', '-release' gives '2023a', '-date' (and the second output) the date of that release, and '-description' mylab's own version.

vertcat.description: Stacks arrays on top of each other, the same as [A; B; ...]. They must have the same number of columns.

view.description: Sets the viewing angle of the current 3-D axes: azimuth az and elevation el in degrees. view(2) looks straight down. Has no effect on 2-D axes.

wait.description: Blocks until the timer t has stopped. For an endless timer this is where the remaining TimerFcn calls happen; it gives up with a warning after 100000 calls.

waitbar.description: Shows progress x between 0 and 1. In a terminal a single text progress bar is redrawn in place; elsewhere nothing is printed. Update the bar by passing its handle h (or nothing, for the most recent bar), and finish with close(h) or delete(h). Example: h = waitbar(0, 'Working'); for k = 1:10, waitbar(k/10, h); end; close(h)

waitfor.description: waitfor(h) behaves like uiwait(h). With a property name it returns at once.

waitforbuttonpress.description: Waits for a mouse click (0) or key press (1) in a plot window. Without a live window it returns 0 at once.

warndlg.description: Prints the message with the label 'Warning' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines.

warning.description: Prints a warning message and carries on. warning('off') or warning('off', 'all') silences all warnings and warning('on') restores them; turning off a single identifier is accepted but has no effect.

waterfall.description: Draws each row of Z as a separate line in 3-D, like a mesh without the lines across rows.

wavread.description: Older form of audioread for WAV files.

wavwrite.description: Older form of audiowrite for WAV files (default 8000 Hz, 16 bits).

wblrnd.description: Random numbers from the Weibull (scale a, shape b) distribution. Parameters may be scalars or arrays of the result's size; trailing arguments give the size, e.g. wblrnd(a, b, 3, 2) or wblrnd(a, b, [3 2]). Invalid parameters give NaN.

web.description: Does not open a browser. Prints a short note with the address, or returns status 0 when an output is requested.

weboptions.description: Options for webread and websave as a struct. Only Timeout (seconds) has an effect.

webread.description: Downloads the content of a web address. Text is returned as a char vector, JSON is decoded when jsondecode is available, and pictures are returned as image arrays. Name-value pairs are added to the address as query parameters. Needs network access: it raises a clear error when the address cannot be reached, and is unavailable when mylab runs in the browser.

websave.description: Downloads a web address into a file and returns the file's full path. Needs network access, like webread.

week.description: Week number within the year (the week containing January 1 is week 1 and weeks start on Sunday), or within the month.

weekday.description: Day of the week as a number, 1 for Sunday through 7 for Saturday, for a datetime array, serial date numbers or date text. The second output is the short day name ('Mon'), or the full name with 'long'.

what.description: Lists the MATLAB files in a folder (the current one by default). With an output it returns a struct with the folder's path and cell arrays m, mat, mlx, classes and packages.

which.description: Tells what a name refers to: 'variable' for a workspace variable, the full path of the .m file for a file function or script, the path of a data file found on the search path, or 'built-in (mylab/name)' for a function built into mylab. Returns '' (and prints a message when used as a command) for an unknown name. '-all' returns every match in a cell array.

who.description: Lists the names of the variables in the current workspace, or returns them as a column cell array.

whos.description: Prints a table of the current variables with their sizes, byte counts and classes. Byte counts are reported for numeric, logical and char arrays only.

width.description: Number of variables (columns) of a table.

wiener2.description: Adaptive noise removal: smooths strongly where the local variance is close to the noise power and little near edges. The noise power is estimated as the average local variance when not given.

winter.description: n-by-3 colormap from blue to green.

workspace.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

wrapTo180.description: Wraps angles in degrees into [-180, 180]; values already in range are kept.

wrapTo2Pi.description: Wraps angles in radians into [0, 2*pi]; positive multiples of 2*pi map to 2*pi.

wrapTo360.description: Wraps angles in degrees into [0, 360]; positive multiples of 360 map to 360.

wrapToPi.description: Wraps angles in radians into [-pi, pi]; values already in range are kept.

writeVideo.description: Appends to the open VideoWriter v: a frame or array of frames from getframe, an image (height-by-width or height-by-width-by-3, uint8 or doubles from 0 to 1), or a 4-D stack of images. Later frames are resized to the size of the first one.

writecell.description: Writes a cell array of numbers and text to a delimited text file, one row of the cell array per line. A file name ending in .xlsx writes an Excel workbook.

writelines.description: Writes text (a string array, cell array or char vector) to a file, one element per line, each followed by a line break.

writematrix.description: Writes a matrix to a delimited text file with full precision, one row per line. The delimiter may be 'comma' (default; tab for .tsv files), 'tab', 'space', 'semi', 'bar' or any single character. Cell arrays, strings and char arrays are written as text, quoted when they contain the delimiter. A file name ending in .xlsx writes an Excel workbook; 'Sheet' and 'Range' choose where.

writetable.description: Writes a table to a delimited text file with a header row of variable names. A file name ending in .xlsx writes an Excel workbook; 'Sheet' and 'Range' choose where.

xcorr.description: Cross-correlation of two vectors (autocorrelation with one input) at every lag from -(N-1) to N-1, or only up to maxlag. scaleopt is 'none' (default), 'biased', 'unbiased' or 'coeff' (peak 1 at lag 0 for autocorrelation). A shorter vector is zero-padded. Only vectors are supported.

xlabel.description: Labels the x axis of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle); accepts the same options as title and returns a Text handle on request.

xlim.description: Sets or returns the x-axis limits of the current axes. An infinite end keeps that side automatic, e.g. xlim([0 Inf]).

xline.description: Draws a vertical line across the current axes at x (several lines for a vector). Options: a line style such as '--r', a label, 'Color', 'LineWidth', 'LineStyle', 'Alpha'.

xlsfinfo.description: Returns a description and the worksheet names (cell array) of an Excel file.

xlsread.description: Reads a worksheet of an Excel file. num is the block of numbers (NaN where a cell holds text or nothing; header rows and columns are dropped), txt a cell array with the text cells and raw a cell array with everything. sheet is a name or number, range is like 'B2:D10'. Works with .xlsx workbooks. With the openpyxl package installed (pip install mylab[excel]) it is used for reading and writing; otherwise a built-in reader and writer handles numbers, text and logical values without formatting. Dates are read as Excel serial numbers. Old .xls files are not supported.

xlswrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix or a cell array of numbers and text to a worksheet of an Excel file, starting at cell A1 or at the first cell of range. Other sheets of an existing file are kept. Works with .xlsx workbooks. With the openpyxl package installed (pip install mylab[excel]) it is used for reading and writing; otherwise a built-in reader and writer handles numbers, text and logical values without formatting. Dates are read as Excel serial numbers. Old .xls files are not supported.

xor.description: Element-wise exclusive OR: true where exactly one of A and B is nonzero.

xtickangle.description: Rotates the x-axis tick labels by angle degrees, or returns the current rotation.

xticklabels.description: Sets the text of the tick labels on the x axis (yticklabels: the y axis) at the current tick positions, in order; extra labels are dropped and missing ones left blank. labels is a cell array, string array or char matrix (numbers are also accepted). With no input, returns the labels as a cell column; 'auto' restores automatic labels.

xticks.description: Puts the x-axis tick marks at the values in v ([] removes them), returns the visible tick positions, or goes back to automatic ticks.

year.description: Year numbers of a datetime array (serial date numbers and date text are also accepted).

years.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many years of 365.2425 days. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of years of 365.2425 days.

ylabel.description: Labels the y axis of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle); accepts the same options as title and returns a Text handle on request.

ylim.description: Sets or returns the y-axis limits of the current axes (the active side with yyaxis). An infinite end keeps that side automatic, e.g. ylim([0 Inf]).

yline.description: Draws a horizontal line across the current axes at y (several lines for a vector). Options: a line style such as '--r', a label, 'Color', 'LineWidth', 'LineStyle', 'Alpha'.

ymd.description: Year, month and day numbers of a datetime array as three numeric arrays.

ytickangle.description: Rotates the y-axis tick labels by angle degrees, or returns the current rotation.

yticklabels.description: Sets the text of the tick labels on the x axis (yticklabels: the y axis) at the current tick positions, in order; extra labels are dropped and missing ones left blank. labels is a cell array, string array or char matrix (numbers are also accepted). With no input, returns the labels as a cell column; 'auto' restores automatic labels.

yticks.description: Puts the y-axis tick marks at the values in v ([] removes them), returns the visible tick positions, or goes back to automatic ticks.

yyaxis.description: Gives the current axes a second y axis on the right. Later plots, labels and limits apply to the chosen side; each side has its own colour.

yyyymmdd.description: Each date as one number whose digits are the year, month and day, such as 20240315.

zeros.description: Array filled with 0. With no size it returns the scalar 0; n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. A class name such as 'int32' or 'single' sets the type. Example: zeros(2, 3) is a 2-by-3 matrix of zeros.

zip.description: Creates a zip archive from a file, folder, wildcard pattern or cell array of those. Names in the archive are relative to rootfolder (the current folder by default). '.zip' is added to the archive name if it has no extension.

zlabel.description: Labels the z axis of the current 3-D axes; ignored on 2-D axes.

zlim.description: Sets or returns the z-axis limits of the current 3-D axes; an infinite end keeps the current limit on that side.

zoom.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

zscore.description: Standardizes data: subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation (N-1 normalization, or N with flag 1) along the first dimension whose size is not 1. Constant data gives zeros.

zticks.description: Sets or returns the z-axis tick positions of 3-D axes.
